documents.content:
# Default Template Overview

The Game project provides playable default gameplay and supplies the project templates. Use it as a starting point for your own game rules, interfaces and resources.

## Entry and modules

Entry retains the static `APP_NAME` for application identity and package filenames. Release version and dev settings belong to `Main.proj` and Pack Options, while mobile and macOS display names come from the System title. See [Packaging](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) for the shared rules.

`Scripts/Entry.lua` initialises the game and enters the native loop. Its module loading order is described in [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>).

Startup calls the following functions explicitly. Requiring their modules does not initialise services:

| Call | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `Source.Locale.Core.Init()` | Loads locale dictionaries before configuration loading and language selection. |
| `Source.Configs.Main.LoadOrCreate()` | Reads `Main.ini`, creating it with default settings when absent. |
| `Source.Data.InitializeRuntime()` | Initialises data services and registers data and Blueprint providers before the first scene. |
| `Source.System.InstallRuntimeProviders()` | Registers the configuration provider before the first scene. |
| `Source.System.Init()` | Applies game and audio configuration and prepares display resources through `GlobalCore.Display` before the native loop. |

Entry also initialises latent graphs and the native System before it constructs `SceneInit`. Register providers once per session. Hot reload does not rerun startup; see [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>). [Runtime Data, Configuration and Saves](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md>) describes the configuration and save locations.

On Android and iOS, returning from the background in the same process resumes the current scene and Lua state without rerunning Entry or catching up on background time; see the [SceneBase lifecycle](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Scenes and System.md#scenebase>).

## Gameplay layout

- `Scripts/Source/MapActors` contains the reusable map Actor classes. `Scripts/Source/Utils` contains gameplay helpers, including the Enemy and GameInstance implementation modules; scenes, business windows and components retain their own directories.
- `Scripts/GlobalFunctions` contains independent Lua Blueprint function libraries. Their paths in graph data begin with `GlobalFunctions.`; the native root module remains separate.
- `Scripts/Internal` contains Live Debug and UI foundations, including the shared window base classes.
- `Scripts/Internal/UI` contains Views generated from `Data/UI/Assets` by Export. Generated UI and locale files are absent from templates and version control; export the project before its first run. Handwritten foundations live in `Internal.UIBase`, and business windows live in `Source.Windows`. See [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>).
- `Scripts/Mixins` contains directly attachable Lua behaviour.
- `Data/Blueprints` contains game-specific Actor classes.
- `Data/General` provides items, enemies, equipment, classes, players, states and special effects.
- `Data/Maps` and `Data/Tilesets` provide the playable world.
- `Engine/` contains the native runtime, modules and dependencies.

[Build and Module Layout](<../../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md>) describes native source ownership and dependencies.

## Template variants

`Cpp` keeps native sources and builds them per project. `Cpp-ffmpeg` adds video support. Standalone variants contain a built runtime for packaging. iOS, HarmonyOS and Android packages are built only from a C++ Source variant, and they use the FFmpeg-enabled C++ Source variant when video is enabled. Changing the Game project does not update an existing project, so regenerate the template or apply the required changes to that project explicitly.

Runtime Lua, `Scripts/stub` declarations and `_meta.lua` file-layer rules are in [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md>).

## Related pages

- [Project Templates](<../../Getting Started/Project Templates.md>)
- [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md>)

documents.content:
# New Game, Title and Scene Flow

The default entry creates `Source.Scenes.SceneInit` and then hands control to the native System loop. SceneInit prepares shared data and advances to the title flow. Loading progress appears in the initialisation screen. The title scene creates the command window for Start Game, Continue, Config and Exit Game. Save/Load and Config are created on first use and reused until the title scene is destroyed.

Scene changes use `GlobalCore.SceneManager`; freezing and transition requests use `GlobalCore.Transition`. Screen flash, shake and tone use `GlobalCore.ScreenEffects`.

### Configure New Game

A new-game action creates or resets the game instance, selects the initial map and player data, and changes to the map scene. `Data/Configs/System.json` stores the player Blueprint under `startPlayerBlueprint` as a path relative to `Data/Blueprints`, and stores the initial region under `startRegion`. These values initialise new games only. Continue restores the player class and the current region saved in the selected slot.

Map entry creates the HUD and Region Title, while optional popups and dialogue wait for their first display. This keeps unused window construction out of scene entry without changing transition durations. Window ownership and reuse are described in [Windows, Menus, Input and Controls](<Windows Menus Input and Controls.md>).

`startMap` may identify an ordinary map, a composite-world manifest such as `World_01/_world.json`, or a placed world child such as `World_01/Map_03.json`. `startPos` is a world coordinate for a manifest target and a child-local coordinate for a child target. The editor presents all three forms through one map tree and stores the selected string path.

### Enter maps and composite worlds

`GlobalFunctions.Scene.GotoMap` follows the same path and coordinate rules. Entering another child of the current world keeps its `WorldGameMap` facade. Unplaced children are invalid destinations.

For a world, `Scene:getGameMap()` and `Actor:getMap()` expose one world-coordinate GameMap facade. Child placements provide passability, Dir4, materials and terrain. Uncovered cells are passable holes. Missing or inconsistent child data is an error.

The facade's `mapName` comes from the required `worldName` in `_world.json`, so UI such as the player HUD identifies the complete world rather than an individual streamed child. Child map JSON retains its own `mapName` for standalone use, but the HUD does not display that name while the child belongs to a loaded world.

On entry, the runtime revalidates the flat world directory, the exact `_world.json`, the required world name, direct JSON child files, placements and layer order. Unrelated non-JSON regular files are ignored, and invalid data fails.

Children progress through `Unloaded`, `Reading`, `Prepared`, `Active` and `Dormant`. Streaming prioritises the Camera neighbourhood and cancels obsolete reads. Only Active Actors simulate. Until every visible placement and Tile chunk is ready, the Camera retains its last complete frame, and colliding movement cannot enter the unprepared area.

Active Actors outside the Camera view continue to simulate without rendering.

With transitions enabled, world entry freezes the outgoing frame until the target viewport and the required Actors, lights and Tile chunks are ready. Required-data failures propagate before release. `blockTransition = true` skips the mask but keeps this readiness barrier. The surrounding preparation remains asynchronous.

`RegionDict` remains floor-transfer data and does not define world composition or streaming.

### Configure Continue

When the title command window is first created, it checks the directory returned by `Engine.getSavePath()`. Any direct entry, including an unrelated file or a subdirectory, selects Continue (`index = 1`); a missing or empty directory selects Start Game (`index = 0`). This check does not parse saves or filter their format. Locale refreshes and returning from Config or Save/Load preserve the current selection. Creating a new title window checks the directory again.

Continue uses `GetSavePath(slot)` to read the plain or encrypted save selected by the native build. It restores game state and opens the appropriate scene. A missing, malformed or unsupported save must follow the explicit not-found or error path instead of silently constructing partial state.

### Preserve scene transitions

Use the System and scene APIs documented in the API reference. The C++ runtime schedules scene changes, so active updates are not destroyed midway through a frame. Windows and temporary resources owned by the outgoing scene are released through its normal lifecycle.

### Customise the title

Edit the Lua scene and window composition and the corresponding data. Keep all text identifiers compatible with [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>).

## Limitations

The Game project does not define a universal save upgrade policy or title-screen design. A released game must define the versions it supports and provide its own presentation and recovery messages.

## Related pages

- [Execution Flow, Events and Variables](<../Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md>)
- [Tilesets, Autotiles and Maps](<../../Editor User Guide/Tilesets Autotiles and Maps.md>)
- [GlobalCore: Scenes and System](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Scenes and System.md>)
- [Run, Debug and Package](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>)

documents.path: docs/en_GB/Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Actors Enemies Items and Equipment.md
documents.content:
# Actors, Enemies, Items and Equipment

## Actors and characters

`Actor` supplies map ownership, position, lifecycle and collision-facing behaviour. Character-style classes add movement and direction. Public class defaults belong on the Lua class table. `init` is reserved for constructor arguments and private runtime state.

`Actor.visible` defaults to `true`. Direct assignment changes the Actor's own flag, and `getVisible` reads it. `setVisible(value, applyToChildren = true)` can also update descendants. An Actor hidden by itself or by an ancestor does not render, block light, collide, overlap, occupy pathfinding cells or accept map-click interaction. Hidden enemies contribute no movement hazards and no Enemy Book entries. A visibility change refreshes the affected caches. Hiding retains the instance, does not stop Tick, and does not rewrite collision or animation settings.

An Actor can configure `emitterComp` as an `Engine.EmitterComponent` to attach a [Common Particle](<../../Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>) effect. It follows the Actor transform and draws immediately before or after its owner in existing list order. Hidden or dormant Actors freeze GPU playback while retaining its state and manual pause setting. Destroy, world eviction, map replacement and Scene exit release the effect. Actor gameplay Tick retains its existing visibility policy.

An Actor can configure `billboardComp` as an [Engine.BillboardComponent](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Gameplay Types.md#billboardcomponent>) to display images and text above its head when the player approaches.

Editor configuration for these fields and attached lights is described in [Actor Components](<../../Editor User Guide/Actor Components/Overview.md>). Default Gameplay Enemy also declares `childActorComp` for its damage readout; see [ChildActor Component](<../../Editor User Guide/Actor Components/ChildActor.md>).

### Conditional appearance

[Source.MapActors.ConditionalActor](<../Source Classes/ConditionalActor.md>) adds `conditionVariable`, `conditionOperator` and `conditionValue`. Select a declared numeric, boolean or string variable, a comparison operator and a value. The editor chooses the value control from the variable type. An empty name disables condition control. Numbers support `==`, `~=`, `>`, `>=`, `<` and `<=`. Booleans and strings support only `==` and `~=`. Invalid data raises an error without conversion.

Enemy, Item, Equip, DoorBase, Teleporter and the Game project's direct map-Actor Blueprints inherit this behaviour. Bottle and Gem keep their Script Mixins. `onCreate` subscribes and evaluates immediately. Later writes to the variable update visibility, and a condition that becomes false hides the Actor again. Hidden Actors keep listening. `onDestroy` and world sleep unsubscribe, while world wake subscribes and reevaluates. Lifecycle overrides must continue the parent event. In graph-mode Blueprints, retain the corresponding [Parent event call](<../Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#parent-event-calls>) in the execution path. EnemyDamageText retains its separate hint behaviour and Tick policy.

See [SceneMap](<../Source Classes/SceneMap.md>) for map loading and lifecycle order, and [ConditionalActor](<../Source Classes/ConditionalActor.md>) for subscriptions and persistence.

### Actors in a composite world

A `WorldGameMap` keeps one world-coordinate Actor registry. Crossing a ready child boundary rehomes the same instance. Holes remain part of the world. Colliding Actors cannot enter unloaded placements, while non-colliding roots sleep and request them asynchronously.

Only roots in Active 32×32-cell chunks simulate or render. Leaving invokes `onWorldSleep()` and returning invokes `onWorldWake(elapsedSeconds)` without replacing `onCreate` or `onDestroy`. Never-activated Prepared roots receive no lifecycle and are absent from gameplay lookup.

Tile and Actor drawing follows the manifest `layerOrder`. Runtime-only layers are appended in first-use order. The player remains last on its layer. Hiding a child Tile layer also hides that layer's Actors from colour and lighting-surface rendering.

`getActorByTag` searches Active Actors and resident roots that slept after activation, without loading a child. Evicted Actors remain absent until reload.

`SceneMap:recordDestroyedActorTag` suppresses that identity in resident and future child payloads without loading an absent child. A suppressed Actor cannot run its lifecycle, become queryable or reappear after eviction. The Actor-taking `recordDestroyedActor` API remains record-only.

## Movement, pathfinding and animation

Scripted [movement and pathfinding](<../Node Functions/Movement.md>) and [door animations](<../Source Classes/DoorBase.md>) return `Engine.AsyncOperation`, allowing Lua scripts and Blueprint flows to wait for completion.

Stopping movement, including disabling it when opening a UI, still processes arrival if the player snaps into a new cell. That cell's overlaps and movement-step effects are not skipped. Danger-driven click-route replanning returns to the last complete cell before stopping. Instant route completion also returns there before stopping, then applies its destination overlaps and collected movement path once.

A* and actual movement apply the same Dir4 edge rule: every newly entered leading cell must allow departure from its source tile and entry through the opposite direction of its destination tile. Click movement reuses the direct A* result for ordinary goals and for one-cell blocked targets. If the moving Actor's footprint prevents that direct result, click movement falls back to searching the target's adjacent cells. A colliding target remains the final attempted step, so its collision interaction still runs. When the fallback is used and the impassable goal has no collider, the player stops at the adjacent cell rather than bumping towards the goal. Pathfinding routes around non-colliding Actors that have an executable `onOverlap`, so they are not entered by accident during transit. When the player explicitly clicks such an Actor as a map destination, the full route to its cell is kept and the player enters it, triggering the overlap interaction — the same way a clicked Teleporter enters its cell and transfers the player.

Passability and pathfinding queries place the Actor footprint exactly on the requested grid cell, preserving its bounds while excluding the pixel offset of an ongoing move. This also keeps movement-hazard line checks independent of movement direction and progress.

World pathfinding crosses loaded child boundaries but treats unloaded children as unavailable without implicit I/O. Holes remain passable with a `nil` top material.

`GameMap.MapViewRect` defines the logical-screen map canvas and defaults to `sf.IntRect.new(192, 32, 416, 416)`. Its position places the canvas, and its size sets both the clipped drawing area and the Camera view size. A map axis smaller than the canvas is centred within that axis, while a larger axis is clamped to its scrollable range. Map rendering, pointer conversion, world and UI positioning, animations, lighting, fog, panorama and weather share this rectangle. Pointer input outside the rectangle is ignored.

Domain, Flank and Blockade Effects grant `Gameplay.Movement.Hazard`. Both movement and `MovementDangerGrid` use `MovementSpecials.Preview`, which dispatches `Event.Movement.QueryHazard`. Keep their spatial rules on that path. Domain includes cells whose Manhattan distance is at most its range (minimum 1): `Domain = 1` reaches the four orthogonally adjacent cells, but not diagonal cells. Its per-round damage respects combat specials, so Magic ignores player defence. Flank requires enemies on opposite adjacent sides, and Blockade affects adjacent cells. Positive contributions add.

After obtaining the Enemy Book, `EnemyDamageText.EnemyDamageHintLevel` uses `Enums.DamageHintLevel` to select no hints (`NONE`, `0`), enemy readouts (`BATTLE`, `1`, default) or enemy and map-cell readouts (`MAP`, `2`). Hints have no gameplay side effects.

Click routes exclude positive-danger cells even while hidden, except for an explicitly clicked destination. Clicking a Domain or Blockade enemy removes only that target's contributions, including its side of a Flank. Collision and overlap targets that the player will not occupy ignore destination-cell danger.

Newly Active world chunks invalidate the danger cache. Full grids materialise only for map hints or click pathfinding. Single-cell queries remain local. A danger revision invalidates movement only when it affects the remaining path or an enterable enemy goal. Invalid routes return to the last complete cell and replan.

## Enemies

An Enemy Blueprint selects an Enemy General Data member. `GeneralDataTypes.Create` copies it into an `EnemyAttributeSet`. `Battler` exposes that set as `attributes` and owns its `AbilitySystemComponent`. Enemy General Data has no member events. Combat behaviour uses explicit Gameplay Abilities and Effects.

`MAXHP` is an enemy's virtual durability, and enemies do not retain mutable `HP`. Player `HP` belongs to `PlayerAttributeSet`, starts at `1000` in Player General Data, and is not stored as a Blueprint attribute override.

Player HP Current is constrained to `0..MAXHP` after modifiers. Permanent MAXHP and LEVEL progression react to Base changes, so temporary Infinite Effects do not alter permanent growth.

Enemy `special` preserves integer counts/ranges, presence-only `""`, the `Vampire` rate, the `FixDmg` number/expression and the `Reborn` class path. Each entry becomes an Infinite `Special.<id>` Effect with a matching tag and focused ability. Combat specials modify combat Gameplay Events. Movement specials use `Event.Movement.QueryHazard` and `Gameplay.Movement.Hazard`.

Every Enemy grants `Ability.Combat.MotaBattle`. Its side-effect-free calculation returns a damage breakdown and numeric `Enums.BattleResultCode` (`WIN`, `CANNOT_DAMAGE` or `LETHAL_COUNTER_DAMAGE`). Collision validates damage, Game Over, reward and State Effect Specs before `CommitResult(result)`. Previews reuse the same calculation without mutation.

Ordinary enemy battles display positive counter damage at the earliest `dmg` time tag of the enemy's attack animation, using a Scene timer. Without that tag or an animation, the damage text appears immediately. HP is still committed immediately, and settlement still waits for both attack animations' visual durations.

`drops` maps each Item Blueprint path to an `sf.Vector2i` offset. Valid drops spawn on the enemy's layer, are persisted as added Actors, and activate their General Data `onDrop` graph through `GeneralDataGraphAbility`. A duplicate placement tag skips that drop. An invalid path or a non-Item Blueprint is an error.

The defeat shatter effect in [Resources, Audio, Video and Effects](<Resources Audio Video and Effects.md#shaders-fog-and-transitions>) is visual only. Defeated enemies stop blocking movement and light immediately when they are destroyed.

After a win and both attack animations, the Enemy Actor Blueprint `onDefeat` event runs. Its completion starts fixed settlement: apply game-variable changes, record and destroy the Enemy, spawn drops or a Reborn replacement, then apply rewards and States. Enemy General Data has no `onDefeat` graph.

An enemy with the `Reborn` special uses that special's non-empty string value as a Blueprint class path. After the original enemy is recorded and destroyed, the replacement spawns on the same map cell and layer with a fresh map-placement tag, runs its normal `onCreate`, and is recorded as an added Actor. Map transfer and save/load therefore keep the original placement destroyed and restore the replacement exactly once. An invalid `Reborn` path is a required-data error.

`afterBattleVarChanges` stores `variableName = { operator, operand }` for declared `int` or `float` variables. Operators are `=`, `+`, `-`, `*`, `/`, `//`, `%` and `**`. The saved shape remains an object whose values are two-element arrays.

Defeat preparation validates the configured operations before combat damage. After `onDefeat`, settlement evaluates them again against current variables through fixed `Engine.Eval` expressions and fresh locals. Stored operators are never executed as source.

Damage previews count counterattacks before the defeating hit. Without healing, maximum HP `H` and positive incoming damage `D` produce `max(ceil(H / D) - 1, 0)` counterattacks. `Vampire = R` heals `floor(counterDamage * R)` after each non-final counterattack. If non-one-shot damage does not exceed healing, the attacker cannot win, and the count is otherwise `ceil((H - D) / (D - healing))`. `First` adds one attack before the player's first attack and cannot heal at full enemy HP. `FixDmg` uses a number directly, or evaluates a string after substituting the current `{m<attribute>}` and `{e<attribute>}` values. The finite non-negative result is floored and added after round and first-strike damage.

When accumulated Domain, Flank or Blockade damage defeats the player, the Game project applies that damage immediately but enters the Game Over scene only after the longest concurrently started attack animation finishes, matching ordinary enemy-battle timing.

## Items

Item member graphs implement `onUse` and `onDrop` as explicitly activated `GeneralDataGraphAbility` instances rather than Actor events. `onUse` targets the Player, and `onDrop` targets the spawned Item Actor. Target-bound nodes therefore use `GameplayEventData.target`. Instance-method nodes retain a visible `self` input; connect the target to it when calling a Player or Item method, because an unset receiver defaults to the graph's `GameplayEventData` owner. Common Functions preserve that owner. Player State nodes belong in `onUse`.

In its `onUse` graph, the EnemyBook item opens the monster handbook through [GlobalFunctions.Scene](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#showenemybook>).

Collision callbacks on the highest occupied tile layer run from the visually topmost Actor to the bottommost Actor. Within one layer, later Actor entries are drawn and triggered first. When several collectible Items occupy one cell, a blocked movement attempt therefore collects the visually topmost Item. Its destruction ends the current collision dispatch, and a later movement attempt collects the next Item. Holding a direction may collect subsequent Items on later fixed updates without requiring a key release.

`GlobalFunctions.Mota.CenterSymmetricTeleport`, `GoUpstairsSamePos` and `GoDownstairsSamePos` provide the reusable logic for CenterSymmetricTeleport, UpstairsTransportation and DownstairsTransportation. The adjacent-floor nodes follow the current region's map order and check the persisted target map at the player's current zero-based coordinates before changing maps. The centre-symmetric node targets `(width - 1 - x, height - 1 - y)` on the current map. Each node exposes `Success` and `Failed` execution branches. Failure resolves `FLY_FAIL` and displays it as a common tip without removing the item. Connect only `Success` to `GlobalFunctions.Player.RemoveItem` when configuring a consumable item graph.

## Equipment

Equipment `attrPlus` becomes a slot-sourced Infinite Effect. It is applied before the explicit `onEquip` graph and removed before `onUnequip`. Slot names must match Class data.

States are Infinite Effects carrying `State.<id>`, stacks, modifiers and abilities. Weak subtracts 1 ATK/DEF per stack with a zero minimum. The HUD shows the Ability System Current value and the Weak stack count, so a base of 10 with two stacks appears as `8 (-2)`. Poisoned adds damage through `Event.Combat.ResolveIncomingDamage`. State graphs listen to `Event.Movement.Step` (`onWalk`) or `Event.State.Trigger.<id>` (explicit hook).

## Runtime references

Use General Data identifiers as stable keys. Runtime application keeps every string verbatim, so class, animation and equipment-slot keys never depend on the selected language. Display names and descriptions may be brace-wrapped localisation identifiers. Resolve them with `LOC` only when presenting them, and resolve them again after a language change. The lookup table is managed by [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>). Renaming an identifier requires updating every reference.

The exact Game schemas and member lists are in the General Data Reference pages, starting with [Class](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data Reference/Class.md>). Practical Bottle, Gem, door and enemy examples are in the Usage Recipes pages, starting with [Consumables](<Recipes/Consumables.md>).

## Limitations

General Data identifiers are project contracts and are not repaired automatically when renamed. The Game project's combat and inventory rules are examples, not mandatory engine behaviour.

## Related pages

- [Ludork Lua Advanced](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>)
- [Class](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data Reference/Class.md>)
- [Source.Battler](<../Source Classes/Battler.md>)
- [Consumables](<Recipes/Consumables.md>)

documents.content:
# Windows, Menus, Input and Controls

The default Lua UI uses JSON assets and generated View trees. Scenes create windows, Views provide their complete controls and nested panes, and the UI manager controls stacking. Business Controllers add model updates and input callbacks.

## Windows and menus

Window views follow the [Declarative UI Runtime Contract](<../Declarative UI/Runtime Contract.md>). Menus keep stable command identifiers separate from displayed text. Long descriptions use the existing wrapping and formatting helpers.

The title's Save/Load and Config windows and the map's optional windows use separate `Internal.UIBase.LazyWindow` handles. Map entry creates the HUD and Region Title directly; Menu, Item, Equip, shops, Save/Load, Config, Enemy Book, Encyclopedia, Floor Teleporter and Player Name are created on their first display. The message window is created by the first message or selection. Opening Menu does not create its Item, Equip, Save/Load or Config windows. Each window's complete authored child tree is built on that first use, then reused until the owning scene is destroyed.

The in-game menu lists Items, Equipments, Files, Config and Return to Title. `WindowMenu.new(player, windows, onExit)` receives the scene's exit action and invokes it after the menu's closing animation. The scene owns the destination and assigns one stacking layer to the menu and its independent sub-windows. Selecting Config opens the shared Config window over the menu and deactivates the command list. Closing the Config window returns focus to the menu.

Every visible default screen has one top-level asset: Init, Title, Game Over, Region Title, HUD, Menu, Config, Message, Item, Equip, Shop, Save/Load, Attribute Shop, Enemy Book, Encyclopedia, Floor Teleporter and Player Name. Multi-pane screens nest their panes under one root, and sibling input hosts reuse the nested lists and scroll boxes.

Top-level window transitions are linear and default to 0.2 seconds. Internal panes and tabs switch immediately. Input is disabled during playback, and close results run after `FadeOut` hides the root. Initialisation and disposal hide immediately.

| UI | Timeline behaviour |
|---|---|
| Default windows and Config | `FadeIn`: centre Scale `0.5` to `1` plus colour; `FadeOut`: colour only. |
| Title command | `FadeIn`: local Y `80` to `0` plus colour. Opening Config or Save/Load does not hide it. |
| Map Menu | `FadeIn`/`FadeOut`: local X `-192` to `0` and back, plus colour. |
| Item and Equip | Menu animations only. Save/Load has both default and Menu pairs, while Config always uses the default pair. |
| Message | `Panel` colour only. |
| Game Over | Colour-only `FadeIn` (0.5 seconds) and `FadeOut` (1 second). Scene switching waits for `FadeOut`, which holds its transparent final frame until scene disposal. |
| Region Title | `Display` holds colour for one second, then fades for one second. |

Related `FadeOut` transitions may run in parallel. Using an inventory item runs its completion callback after the item window is hidden; an open menu then closes and restores movement once no blocking window remains.

Assets include representative `#TAB` and `#ITEM` children and Game visuals. Dynamic collections replace list placeholders before display, and Controllers localise TabView items without changing their count. Enemy Book and Encyclopedia use `CharacterView`. The runtime passes the real actor snapshot, while native code owns cropping, animation, scale and Shader/Hue effects. Enemy Book cells use their authored dimensions; Controllers measure names and special tags against those areas, including on language changes.

`Source.Windows` modules export UI classes through `Ui.DefineWindow`, with business behaviour in private Controllers. The title's `WindowCommand` binds the four existing rows in `Parts/Title/CommandWindow`; its parent `Title` asset owns placement. UI authoring and file layout are described in [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>).

When a selectable list gains focus, the current selection scrolls into view while the mouse pointer stays in place. This also applies when opening a window, switching panes or returning to a parent list.

On mobile, tapping a different row moves the selection cursor without confirming. Tapping the currently selected row confirms it. Dragging the list scrolls without confirming a row. This applies to the title command window and the shared Save/Load slot list as well as other selectable windows.

On the title screen, an open Config or Save/Load window prevents the underlying command window from receiving any part of the same touch gesture.

The shared `Parts/Shared/WindowChrome` asset provides a 16 × 16 return button on the top-left border, outside `Content`. `WindowBase` binds it, and cancellable windows enable it with `windowOptions.returnButton = true` and implement `Controller:onReturn()` with the same state-aware step used by other Cancel inputs. That shared return step plays the System CancelSE once, so a second Cancel source must not play it again. Multi-pane groups expose the button only on the active interactive pane. Hidden, inactive or suppressed windows do not expose it.

`WindowChrome` also places an `Engine.GamepadHintBar` on the bottom border, outside `Content`, and owns its text style. It stays empty unless a gamepad is connected and the window supplies hints. A window sets up to three `Engine.GamepadHint` entries with `setGamepadHints`, toggles one with `setGamepadHintEnabled`, reads `getGamepadHintCount` and `isGamepadConnected`, and handles completions through `setOnGamepadHintTriggered`. The separate `Parts/Shared/WindowPauseMark` asset fixes pause-mark size and placement; `WindowBase` supplies its skin animation and visibility. See [GamepadHintBar](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Interactive and Declarative UI Controls.md#gamepadhintbar>) for rendering and the one-second long-press.

Static command rows store a `localeKey`, while dynamic rows store literal `text`. A row must never define both. The row resolves `localeKey` when it refreshes, so a language change can update the existing controls without replacing their callbacks or cursor state. The title commands, in-game menu, save/load tabs, shop tabs and details, and a visible map-region title update immediately when the runtime language changes.

Whenever a reusable selectable window begins a new open session, its selectors start at zero and scroll to the top. An empty selector uses `nil`. This behaviour applies to the in-game menu, item and equipment windows, shops, Config and Enemy Book. Focus changes and in-place refreshes within that session preserve the selection.

Load `Enums.ShopMode` for the public `WindowShop:setMode(mode)` values `BUY = "buy"` and `SELL = "sell"`. Item, Equip and Save/Load opening calls use `Enums.WindowTransitionProfile.DEFAULT` (`"Default"`) or `.MENU` (`"Menu"`) as their transition profile.

The shop keeps its two-column item list focused while Q/E, LB/RB, mouse or touch switches Buy/Sell. Switching tabs resets the cursor and scroll, while a transaction refresh preserves a still-valid selection. Buy and Sell cells show the icon and current owned count, and details show the localised name, description, a localised `Price` label and the right-aligned price. Selling grants `floor(price / 2)` GOLD and omits zero-price results. Buy-only shops hide the tabs and centre the remaining panes. Cancel closes the shop. Closing restores the prior movement state and blocks map input for one frame.

Overflowing lists use `Engine.ScrollBox`. It clips rendering and hit testing, scrolls only overflowing axes, and keeps keyboard/controller selection visible. Native edge indicators show the remaining content. See [Engine: Layout and Image Controls](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Layout and Image Controls.md>).

The message window uses a full-screen Canvas and a transparent `FunctionalImage` to consume one click or tap for plain-message confirmation. Choice mode disables that layer, so blank-space clicks cannot select an option. Its maximum of four options fits directly in the panel without a ScrollBox. `SceneMap` only blocks map input while dialogue is active.

`SceneMap` owns one `LocaleChanged` subscription for its long-lived map windows. Active dialogue retains the raw speaker, message or options, explicit `localeArgs`, and snapshots of node-local and instance variables. It reruns template localisation and localises string `localeArgs`. It then applies those arguments and the two variable snapshots before updating the existing `WindowMessage` controls. Item and equipment details, shop tabs and details, attribute shops, Enemy Book, `WindowEnemyEncyclopedia`, and Teleporter (`WindowFloorTeleporter`) likewise refresh localised text in place while preserving their current selection, mode, focus and preview state. Hidden windows resolve the active language when they next open, while Config, save-slot and player-HUD controllers keep their own subscriptions. The player HUD also subscribes to `AbilitySystemChanged` and `PlayerChanged` from `Enums.EventKey`, ignores payloads whose `owner` is another battler, and refreshes only the affected controls when a signature of the current player changes. Change payloads use `Enums.AbilitySystemChangeKind` (`Attribute`, `State`) or `Enums.PlayerChangeKind` (`Inventory`, `Name`, `Map`); their shared record is declared as `Source.Configs.EventChangePayload`.

Language changes, loaded-player rebinding, visibility queries and input checks only inspect already-created windows through `peek()`. An unused window does not block map input or acquire focus, and its factory reads the current player, game instance and configuration when it is eventually opened. Destroying a scene disposes its handles, releasing existing windows without constructing unused ones.

The Teleporter opens with the current map's floor entry selected and scrolled into view, falling back to the first entry when the current map is absent. An empty list uses `nil` and hides the preview. Opening resolves the final floor selection before generating its single preview. Telepoint selection starts at the first entry. Its left slot alternates between the floor and telepoint lists, and cancelling telepoint selection restores the floors. The telepoint list scrolls without moving the right-side preview. A composite manifest remains one floor identity, with child maps composed at world offsets.

Stair transfers arrive at the nearest stair of the opposite direction: up to `Down`, down to `Up`. Set the `stairDirection` enum in each stair Blueprint; ordinary `None` teleporters are excluded from these arrivals. See [Source.MapActors.Teleporter](<../Source Classes/Teleporter.md>).

Telepoints are discovered through stair transfers or `Teleporter:goToMap(mapPath, position, record)` with `record` omitted or `true`, even before the Teleporter item is acquired. `goToMap` records the source actor's offset position and the exact destination tile on their respective maps, without searching for a destination stair. Passing `false` records neither endpoint. The window lists only the current map's region; a map without a configured region has an empty floor list. Opening the window or approaching stairs does not record a visit. Record structure and deduplication are described in [Runtime Data, Configuration and Saves](<Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md>).

Telepoint labels resolve the recorded tag through `LOC`. Empty or automatically generated tags use the localised `POINT` number format, and missing translations retain the raw tag.

Keyboard, mouse and touch selection update the destination and preview before confirmation. The preview keeps a fixed scale and stays within map bounds, centring axes smaller than the view. Composite previews use the full manifest bounds.

Floor previews use static display records without constructing gameplay Actors or instantiating event graphs. They preserve the configured texture, first-frame rectangle, layer, position, translation, rotation, scale, origin, hue and shader; shader `time` is fixed at `0`. Shader and hue can be combined. Actor constructors, lifecycle callbacks, combat systems, particles, sounds and dynamic damage text do not run, so appearances created only by gameplay scripts are absent.

Destroyed tags and their child trees are filtered before display records or textures are created. Added and moved records and terrain destruction are restored; declarative `childActorComp` children retain their offsets, tags and ancestor visibility without running component callbacks. Ordinary maps retain their region-hiding rules, and composite children retain world offsets.

The static records evaluate [ConditionalActor](<../Source Classes/ConditionalActor.md>) visibility against current game variables, including on other floors and composite-world children, without subscriptions on preview objects. Changes to variables used by cached previews invalidate their textures; the next draw reevaluates the cached records. Reopening the window clears its preview models, textures and class display templates.

Attribute shops expose display snapshots through `getOffers()` and validate purchases through `purchaseAttribute(key)`. A scalar price reference is shared by all offers, while an array sets per-offer prices. A purchase increments the corresponding price.

Dialogue, tutorial and window APIs return `Engine.AsyncOperation`. See [Scene operations](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#lua-waiting-and-results>) for completion results and [Lua asynchronous tasks](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>) for sequential waiting.

### Map introduction

`Map_01` uses the invisible `BP_MapIntroduction` Actor to introduce the HUD menu portrait and representative Actors after the map transition. It runs the guides in order, then records and destroys itself.

`Source.Configs.Tutorial` maps each key to `{ rect: sf.IntRect, text: string }`. Rectangles use fixed logical screen coordinates and do not follow Actors. The `BP_MapIntroduction` graph lists the tutorial keys in its `ForEach` input and calls `ShowTutorial` for each key. The scene component reads the requested configuration and manages presentation; it does not choose tutorials by map name or Actor tags. Update the rectangles when changing the layout.

The opening contracts to the rectangle in 0.25 seconds, with interaction blocked. A 40%-opaque grey curtain covers the rest of the game screen, including the HUD and margins. The border flashes once, and [confirmation](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md#inputcapture>) becomes available after contraction.

Explanations use size 12, outlined text and short localised sentences, refreshed when the language changes. Left-aligned text starts at the rectangle's bottom-middle, shifts left to stay within the right edge, and moves above the top-middle if it cannot fit below. Text wider than the screen wraps first. See [tutorial nodes](<../Node Functions/Scene.md#tutorials>) for invocation.

### Player name window

The NPC beside the starting point in `Map_01` opens `WindowPlayerName` and pauses map input until it closes. Activate the input to edit with the Confirm action. Tab/Shift+Tab and directional actions move between the input and Confirm.

Confirm stays visible for every input device. Mouse and touch activate the button. Keyboard Enter/Space applies the name when Confirm has focus, otherwise starts editing. The asset binds Confirm to a one-second X long-press (`gamepadButton = "X"`, `gamepadLongPress = true`) and does not populate the window hint bar. A only starts editing, including while Confirm has focus. Holding X applies the name from any focus in the active window. See [Button](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Runtime Values and Functional Controls.md#button>) for the empty-texture and hint appearance. The return button or Cancel discards the draft; while editing, Cancel (B or Escape) first ends editing and a second Cancel closes the window. Completing the mobile input dialog only updates the draft. Invalid names disable Confirm; see [Source.MapActors.Player](<../Source Classes/Player.md>) for the validation rules. The HUD shows the confirmed name above the level, shortened to fit.

### Region-aware map previews

When `GameMap.HideDisconnectedRegions` is enabled, Enemy Book excludes Actors hidden by the current region before grouping and deduplication. Floor Teleporter previews follow the same rule: the current floor uses the player's position, and another floor uses the selected destination cell. Selecting a different destination region or changing terrain invalidates the preview cache. Region hiding affects presentation only; telepoint records and transfer destinations are unchanged. See [Global.GameMap](<../Global and Core Modules/Global APIs/GameMap.md#disconnected-regions>).

## Input

`Source.Configs.HotKey` maps native keys to a `Scene`, a `Filter` and optional `FunctionWhenPressed` / `FunctionWhenReleased` callbacks. Each callback receives the scene instance.

Runtime input comes from the C++ input service. Use documented key, mouse, controller and injected-input APIs rather than reading editor state. Embedded Windows mode forwards compatible input through the runtime protocol, while standalone games use the native window directly.

On Android and HarmonyOS, the host converts the system Back button or gesture into one Cancel/Escape pulse instead of closing or backgrounding the app. This conversion remains separate from HarmonyOS external-keyboard forwarding, which sends ordinary SFML-mapped keys as scancode edges, adds logical-key edges where they can be resolved, and preserves their modifier state. Two-finger touch remains a separate right-click cancellation gesture. System Back and two-finger touch both reach the focused window's `onReturn()`, but only the latter emits right-mouse input.

Physical Enter and Space use the Confirm action, while Escape uses Cancel. Keyboard press and release are edge events; see [Engine: Input and Services](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md>).

Controller buttons use the logical `Engine.JoystickButton.getA()` through `getShare()` values. Confirm is A/Cross and Cancel is B/Circle. Per-controller resolution, mappings and hints are in [Engine: Input and Services](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Input and Services.md>).

Default movement and menu directions use only left-stick `X`/`Y` and D-pad `PovX`/`PovY`. Horizontal wins when `|X| >= |Y|`, and vertical wins otherwise. Exact 45-degree input is horizontal. This same sector rule drives triggered navigation and held movement, and right-stick and trigger axes cannot steal the direction.

`WindowSelectable` owns the default Cancel key and the right-button close behaviour. Derived windows return unhandled input to it, so each edge produces one Cancel sound and one close transition.

## Focus and navigation

Keyboard and controller navigation needs an explicit focus order. A disabled or hidden control must not remain the active focus target.

## Configuration controls

Config opens on Graphics with its first row focused. Q/E, LB/RB, mouse hover and touch taps switch tabs and play CursorSE. Each tab keeps its cursor and scroll during that open session. Reopening resets all tabs, while a locale refresh preserves them.

Switching tabs silently collapses an open DropBox. Cancel and the return button also collapse it first, then close Config on the next input. [Game Settings Reference](<Game Settings Reference.md>) defines the settings.

On mobile, a Slider tap sets its value on release. After the drag threshold, horizontal movement belongs to the Slider, while vertical or tied movement belongs to the Config list. Gesture ownership remains fixed until release, and the list scrolls only when its content exceeds the visible area.

An expanded Config DropBox overlays the settings rows and owns input until it collapses or Config closes. Either restores parent-list input. A height-limited popup scrolls internally, and mobile touch uses preview-then-confirm. See [Engine: Interactive and Declarative UI Controls](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Interactive and Declarative UI Controls.md>).

Save/Load uses one shared slot list. Switching the Load/Save tabs preserves its cursor, scroll and detail. Reopening defaults to Load and the newest existing save, or slot zero when none exists; map hotkey S opens Save instead. Cancel closes it. Title load-only mode omits the tabs and centres the remaining panes.

Exact UI and input APIs are in the API reference, starting with [GlobalFunctions.Container](<../Node Functions/Container.md>). Game-localised labels follow [Game Localisation Workflow](<../../Plug-in Development and Installation/Official Plug-ins/Game Localisation Workflow.md>). Editor language switching is not part of this runtime section.

## Related pages

- [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>)
- [Engine: Interactive and Declarative UI Controls](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/Engine/Interactive and Declarative UI Controls.md>)

# Resources, Audio, Video and Effects

## Resource paths

Stored resources use exact-case `/Game/Assets/...` paths with `/` separators and extensions. Generic managers require that complete form. Category helpers such as `loadCharacter("actors/Hero.png")` and `playSE("cursor.ogg")` accept only category-relative arguments and add their own prefix.

The runtime reads loose files and `.ldpak` entries through the same logical paths, with streaming and seeking for music and video. Standard filesystem APIs and LuaSF file constructors do not resolve paths inside archives.

## Animation caches

Animation sources live in `Data/Animations`. `Engine.getAnimationCacheRoot()` creates `Cache/Animations` under `Engine.getUserDataPath()` for both loose and archived Data. On Windows, the user-data root is the runtime working directory. Other platforms use their application user-data location.

Initialisation generates missing `.anim.json`/`.anim.ldc` caches and rebuilds them when source data or referenced frame assets change, preserving paths relative to `Data/Animations`. Caches are disposable and excluded from templates and player packages. Sources are decoded through `Engine.decodeData` and caches are written through `Engine.saveData`; `.anim.ldc` contains binary data, with no intermediate JSON conversion. Delete old caches containing compressed JSON so initialisation regenerates them.

## Audio

Music, sound effects and voices have independent enable flags and volumes in `Main.ini`. The GlobalFunctions Manager group provides the gameplay-facing helpers. Handle missing optional sound paths deliberately. Repeatedly loading the same resource under different path spellings defeats caching.

Audio effects used by the gameplay Manager and Blueprint nodes are Lua DSP processors defined by `Source.Utils.AudioEffects`. The Game project provides the case-sensitive `Echo`, `Distortion`, `Underwater` and `BehindWall` presets. Their defaults remain a 0.3-second/0.5-decay echo, a 2.0-drive/0.7-threshold distortion, a 0.7-depth/0.3-bubble underwater effect, and a 900-Hz/0.35-transmission behind-wall filter.

`GlobalFunctions.Audio.SetEffect(audioType, effect)` resolves the name with `AudioEffects.Get` and stores the resulting attacher independently for the `Sound`, `Voice` or `Music` category. Metadata presents both parameters as drop-downs. Selection does not create a processor and does not modify a source that is already playing. Each later source invokes the attacher, which creates an isolated audio Lua state and a fresh processor for that source. Select the literal string `nil` to clear the preset for future playback. Any other unknown name raises immediately. `Source.Utils.AudioEffects` is the sole preset registry, so a change to the preset registry also requires an update to the `SetEffect` metadata drop-down. Effect selection is not part of `SoundFilter` or `MusicFilter`.

For a non-empty preset, source creation captures the current playback-device sample rate before play. An active source keeps those coefficients after device rerouting, so start a new Manager playback to use the new rate. The attacher must install exactly one non-empty processor, so a selected preset cannot play dry. SFML stores one processor per source. Presets are not chained or mixed.

After hot reload, start a new playback to use updated audio code; see [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#lua-hot-reload>). Playing sources and buffered tails continue unchanged.

`Echo` drains its buffered tail after a natural end of stream. An explicit Manager stop, a dialogue skip or shutdown discards the remaining tail. Direct `sf.SoundSource:setEffectProcessor` use is a separate low-level API, and it does not receive the Manager isolation, EOS or cancellation protocol.

`GlobalFunctions.Scene.ShowVoiceMessageByTag` and `ShowVoiceMessage` capture the exact Voice handle started by that call for the lifetime of their dialogue. When the dialogue finishes, their latent condition stops that handle before `FinishedDialogue` resumes downstream Blueprint execution. A following `SetEffect` therefore configures the next Voice. Leaving or destroying a map scene also stops the current global Voice. Ordinary message nodes do not change Voice playback.

## Shaders, fog and transitions

User-authored Actor and layer shaders remain optional. Check `sf.Shader.isAvailable()` or `sf.Shader.isGeometryAvailable()` when gameplay can run without them. Built-in weather and fog instead require their shared cross-platform shader assets and propagate load or compilation failures. World entry prewarms the shared map compositor for the current viewport and repeats when regional geometry changes. HarmonyOS skips explicit prewarming and compiles each shader during its first normal draw, after the complete render state and uniforms are bound. HarmonyOS OpenGL ES treats unversioned shaders as ESSL 1.00 and preserves the public `setUniform("texture", ...)` name. Explicit versions must match the backend.

Actor fragment shaders are cached by exact shader path for the lifetime of the Engine runtime. Actors using the same path therefore receive the same `sf.Shader` from `Actor:getShader()`. The standard `texture`, `time`, `textureSize` and `textureRect` uniforms are rebound immediately before each Actor map or preview draw. Other uniforms remain shared mutable shader state and must not be treated as persistent per-Actor values. A shader that fails to load is not cached. The affected Actor reports `Actor:hasShaderError()` and continues through the existing fallback rendering path.

Fog is generated on the GPU from world coordinates, absolute time and a deterministic seed. Map data store an object with `enabled`, `colour`, `density`, `scale`, `velocity`, `turbulence` and `seed`; there is no fog texture. The shared renderer composites fog after materials and lighting, before foreground weather and particles. Lit fog responds to scene light; Unlit fog retains its configured colour. Each map session owns its fog state.

See [FogController](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalCore/Map and Fog.md#fogcontroller>) for fog fields, defaults and accepted values.

Map panorama data uses an optional-string protocol. `panorama` is a canonical `/Game/Assets/...` path, and panorama is disabled when it is missing, `nil` or blank. The image Cover-scales to fill `GameMap.MapViewRect` while preserving the aspect ratio, and then crops the overflow using the Camera origin as a fraction of `(mapPixels - viewPixels)` on each axis. An axis with no camera travel uses `0.5`. Transparent tiles and canvas margins reveal the panorama multiplied by ambient light only, while point lights still apply to opaque tiles. A missing texture is a required-resource failure.

### Composite-world environment

A world manifest may define global fog and a global panorama, but not BGM, BGS, audio filters or ambient light. Global fog covers the world bounds, including holes. Child fog is clipped to its placement and sampled in the same world coordinates and time. It is composed after global fog in stable placement order; matching settings remain continuous across adjacent regions. Evicting a child removes its regional fog until reload. Global panorama covers the world Camera using the world size for scroll. A child's `panorama` applies only when that child is loaded as a standalone map.

BGM, BGS and ambient light follow the child beneath the player. Audio switches fade for 0.5 seconds, and returning during a fade-out restores that source. Later ambient changes also blend for 0.5 seconds, using white in holes. World fog and panorama remain active there.

The Game project's advanced enemy-defeat effect is controlled by the global class setting `Enemy.DefeatShatterEffectEnabled`, which defaults to `true` and is not a Blueprint field. Its shader renders a snapshot as world-space logical-pixel fragments scattering radially outward from the centre for about 0.65 seconds. The defeated enemy has already been recorded and destroyed, so the snapshot does not affect passability, collision or light blocking. When the setting is `false` or `sf.Shader.isAvailable()` is false, the enemy disappears immediately instead.

## Video

Video playback requires an FFmpeg-enabled project or template. Keep files beneath `Assets/Videos` and reference them as `/Game/Assets/Videos/...`. Loose files and entries in the root `Assets.ldpak` share the same seekable playback contract. Android supports MOV, H.264/AAC, swscale and swresample, but not network, JNI, MediaCodec or hardware acceleration. Build and distribution requirements are in [Project Templates](<../../Getting Started/Project Templates.md#ffmpeg-option>).

Call `Video.PlayVideo(videoFileName, mute, skipable, subtitleFileName)` through `require("GlobalFunctions.Video")`. The optional fourth argument is a project-relative `Data/Subtitles/...json` path; omission or an empty string preserves video-only playback.

```lua
local Video = require("GlobalFunctions.Video")
Video.PlayVideo("/Game/Assets/Videos/intro.mp4", false, true, "Data/Subtitles/intro.json")
```

[Subtitle data](<../../Editor User Guide/Video Subtitles.md>) contain `type: "subtitle"` and a `sections` array. Each section supplies start/end times in seconds and either a shared string array or a language-to-array dictionary. Dictionary content selects the current game language, then `en_GB` only if the requested key is missing; an existing empty array suppresses subtitles. Subtitles follow the video clock and display centred at the bottom of the viewport using the default font, white text and a black outline.

## Limitations

Shader availability is determined by the runtime graphics environment, and a successful editor preview does not guarantee equivalent target hardware support.

World lighting uses world coordinates, so Actor lights illuminate and cast shadows across child boundaries. Tile masks remain clipped to their placements, and holes contribute neither surfaces nor blockers. Fixed map light records and their map management APIs are removed; attach a `LightComponent` to an Actor to create a light.

Editor ordinary maps, world canvases and thumbnails use the same native map renderer. Unlit is the default: white ambient and no direct light or shadows, with opacity, reflections, shaders and hue preserved. Lit uses actual light inputs, and the editor world canvas uses each child's ambient colour. Panorama and fog have independent display switches. The game retains its player-region ambient transition described above.

## Related pages

- [Common Particles](<../../Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>) — independent GPU emitter assets for Actor Components and UI; existing code-driven particles and effects remain available.
- [Project Templates](<../../Getting Started/Project Templates.md>)
- [Run, Debug and Package](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>)
- [GlobalFunctions Lua API](<../Global and Core Modules/Core Modules/GlobalFunctions.md>)

# Runtime Data, Configuration and Saves

## Configuration

Optional [remote account dictionaries](<../../Simple Server/Native Client API.md>) are a separate service. They do not automatically upload, download or replace the local saves described here; gameplay chooses which fields to read and write.

`Data/Configs` contains game configuration JSON. `Main.ini` contains mutable launch and user settings. Use the configuration APIs and editor fields so unknown sections and keys survive a round trip.

Resource-valued Config `file` fields store complete `/Game/Assets/...` paths, while `base` and `ext` only constrain the selector. Data references remain separate. `System.json` keeps `startPlayerBlueprint` relative to `Data/Blueprints` with `root = "Data"` and converts it to `Data.Blueprints.*`. `startRegion` names the initial region. Both affect new games only, and saves retain their player class and region.

Cell size is fixed by the compiled engine (`32` by default). Read it through `Engine.GetCellSize()`. `System.json` and the System Config editor do not configure it. A leftover `System/cellSize` field is neither used nor editable, and it is not converted into a runtime setting.

Game Lua configuration modules live under `Scripts/Source/Configs` and are loaded through `Source.Configs.*`.

`Source.Locale.Core.DEFAULT_LANGUAGE` is the shared initial and fallback language (`en_GB`); `Source.Configs.Main` uses the same value. `Source.Configs.MapConstants.WORLD_MANIFEST_FILE` defines the composite-world filename (`_world.json`). Data readers and saves use the suffixes from `Engine.ResourceFileConstants`.

Initial data keys use paths relative to their category directory, with `/` separators and only the final extension removed. Dots in directory and file names are preserved: `folder.v1/item.v2.json` becomes `folder.v1/item.v2`. Animation keys remove the complete `.anim.json` cache suffix.

In editor mode, `LUDORK_EDITOR=1` selects the project `Main.ini`. A normal packaged run uses the platform user-data location, with the packaged configuration as the initial source where applicable.

An Android package mirrors its immutable runtime assets into `filesDir/ludork/runtime/<runtime-hash>` before native startup. Mutable configuration and saves use `filesDir/ludork/user-data`. They are never written back into that versioned runtime directory and do not require external-storage permission.

## Runtime state

Keep immutable definitions in Blueprint, Config or General Data files, and keep mutable play-session state on the game instance, actors or components. Avoid writing transient state back into source JSON.

`Data.GetClassData(path)` exposes the shared session definition; see [Execution Flow, Events and Variables](<../Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#class-definitions-and-session-lifetime>).

Construct General Data Attribute Sets with `Source.Configs.GeneralDataTypes.Create`. Load type keys from `Enums.GeneralDataKey` and member keys from `Enums.GeneralData.<TypeName>`, such as `Enums.GeneralData.Item`. The editor resolves these enums from live, possibly unsaved project data. Saving regenerates their runtime sources alongside `Enums.Animation` and `Enums.Particle`; runtime callers see the saved modules. The [General Data and Text Config](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md>) page describes value conversion and defaults.

### Static Actor display data

`Source.Data.GetActorPreviewData(classPath, classVarChanges?)` returns `Source.Data.ActorPreviewData`, or `nil` for an empty class path. Invalid class paths raise an error. It resolves inherited Blueprint and Script Mixin defaults, then applies declared display and condition overrides with their existing typed conversion. Unknown override names fail; unrelated gameplay values and `BlueprintOnly` overrides are not applied. A resolved class must derive from `Engine.Actor`.

The record contains texture and shader paths, the configured first-frame `rect`, `translation`, rotation in degrees, `scale`, `origin`, `visible`, `hue`, condition fields, and optional recursive `child` with its `childOffset`. Declarative `childActorComp` supplies child class and offset; cyclic child references fail. Each call returns independent records and copied mutable `sf` rectangles and vectors, so callers cannot alter shared class defaults or cached templates.

Extraction does not construct gameplay Actors, instantiate event graphs, load the referenced textures, dispatch component or lifecycle callbacks, or initialise combat state. `Source.Data.ClearActorPreviewCache()` discards the class display templates without altering shared class definitions; clearing the floor-preview cache calls it automatically.

### Players

`GameInstance` stores player order in `_playerKeys` and player objects in `_players`, keyed by the stable Player General Data key from `Player.ID`. Player keys must be non-empty and unique. `getPlayers()` returns the live keyed dictionary, while `getPlayerKeys()` returns the live ordered key array. Its first key identifies the primary player used by `getPlayer()`. `getPlayerByIndex()` resolves a zero-based index through the same order, `setPlayer(playerKey)` moves an existing key to the first position, and `setPlayerByClass(playerClass)` does the same after resolving the class path.

Saves preserve the same structure as sibling `playerKeys` and `players` fields. `playerKeys` defines the order, and every key must have exactly one matching entry in `players` with the same restored `Player.ID`. `addPlayerByClass(playerClass, mapPath, position)` appends a party member and stores a required map path and cell for that key. `removePlayerByClass` also drops that key's stored map.

Each Player saves every numeric Attribute Set Base under `attr` from `getNumericAttributeBases()`. Derived Current values are not saved, and non-numeric attributes are rebuilt from Player General Data. Values must be finite and follow the generated `int` or `float` schema. Missing keys in an older save keep the restored member's initial Base.

Saves retain inventory/equipment counts, equipped IDs and State stacks. Loading restores all Base values first, then Item abilities, equipment Effects and State Effects without running initial-equipment or member graphs. Handles, derived Current values, transient Effects, ability specs and tags are not saved. Persistent additions need their own stable record and rebuild step.

Player saves require a string `customName` alongside `attr`. `""` selects the localised General Data default. Non-empty values must already be trimmed and satisfy the rules in [Source.MapActors.Player](<../Source Classes/Player.md>).

### Game variables

The runtime reads initial values from the generated `Scripts/Source/Configs/GameVariables.lua`. Save the edits in [General Data](<../../Editor User Guide/General Data and Text Config.md#game-variable-manager>) before starting the runtime. List and dictionary initial values are ordinary Lua tables rather than Standard containers, and an empty table serialised through JSON is not guaranteed to retain its array or object shape.

`GameInstance:init` deep-copies the generated runtime map, so every new game receives independent mutable initial values. The Game project declares `MTExample = 0` and `ShopPrice = 20`. Runtime systems may still create dynamic names, but only editor-declared names appear in `InstVar` selectors.

A loaded save replaces the newly constructed instance's variable table with the table stored in that save. Generated initial values therefore apply to new games only. Changing, adding or removing a declaration does not migrate or merge an existing slot. Changing a declaration's type also resets its project initial value, but not the values already stored in saves.

Variable snapshots include the current logical values of monitored fields. `deepcopy` excludes monitor proxies and subscriptions, so ConditionalActor listeners stay within the live game instance. After restoring records, `onCreate` subscribes to the restored variables and recomputes visibility. No extra save fields are needed.

### Map Actor identity

The placement `tag` in map JSON becomes the Actor's map-persistence tag. `GameMap:getActorByTag` and `GameInstance` persistence records identify Actors only through `Actor:getMapTag()`, and `Actor.tag` remains independent. Actors without a map tag are not recorded, and map paths are normalised for these records.

Runtime-spawned Actors that must survive a map rebuild are stored through the added-Actor record using their own generated map-placement tag. When such an Actor is later destroyed, its destroyed record suppresses the stored addition. Reborn enemies use this existing pair of records rather than reusing the original placement tag.

World runtime tags use `<child-file-stem>.runtime_default_<N>` in placements and `<world-directory>.runtime_default_<N>` in holes. All tags remain reserved for the world lifetime, and conflicts fail. Editor tags are unique world-wide and stable across map renames.

Map `BPClassVarChanged` and persisted `classVarChanges` contain only values for declared class fields. The editor and runtime resolve their types through metadata, Script Mixins and Blueprint `attrDefs`; an instance cannot introduce a field or change its type. Unknown override names and values that do not match the resolved schema fail loading. Enum overrides store the underlying scalar, and declared vectors and records use their typed conversion when applied.

### Composite-world persistence

The primary player's `map` entry stores the manifest path even when entry used a child. Player, added, moved and destroyed records use that identity, world coordinates and global tags. Conflicting added or moved records fail loading.

Added Actors restore at `actorPositions[tag]` when it is present, and otherwise at their original position. Destroyed tags are skipped. Placement Actors restore with their child payload without distant child I/O, while hole Actors may restore immediately.

`worldMovedActors` owns authored roots outside their definition child, storing identity, owner, layer overrides and world position. They rebuild only at that owner. Returning or destruction removes the moved record.

Destroying a tag removes its moved record and suppresses authored, added, resident and in-progress instances without loading absent children. Suppressed tags stay reserved, and invalid records and collisions fail.

Terrain records use child paths and local coordinates. They apply when that child builds and update only its affected live layer. Holes cannot own terrain changes.

A world save requires `worldMovedActors` when any stored player map is a world manifest. Moved snapshots preserve reconstruction identity, class-variable overrides, layer and position, but not arbitrary instance fields, private Lua state or timer progress. Persist those separately, or recover the time through `onWorldWake`.

## Saves

[Live Debug](<../../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#live-debug>) does not write project documents and does not change the save schema, slots or persistence records. A save during that run can keep gameplay state that live edits affected.

The Game project save schema remains v1, serialised as the number `1`. Only the current structure and version are supported. `SaveCodec` rejects incompatible saves without migration.

Save schema versions are independent of application release versions and the packaging dev checkbox. A new save format under development uses `vN-dev`; freeze its structure and change it to `vN` before release. After releasing v1, start `v2-dev` only when the save format actually needs a version change, then freeze it as v2 for release. Ordinary game releases do not automatically advance the save version. This naming convention does not change the current numeric `1` format or introduce migration.

`telepoints` maps normalised map paths to ordered `{ position = {x, y}, tag = "raw tag" }` records. Runtime positions use `sf.Vector2u`, and tags remain unlocalised strings. `GameInstance:recordTelepoint(mapPath, position, tag)` preserves the first record for each map and position pair, and `getTelepoints(mapPath)` returns the records. World records use the manifest identity and world coordinates.

`triggeredTutorials` contains unique tutorial keys in display-start order: a native `list<string>` at runtime and a JSON array in saves. Its empty array shape is preserved when writing. Loading accepts the native JSON reader's `n` length field, requires it to match the element count, and rejects holes or invalid keys. `hasTriggeredTutorial(key)` queries history; `recordTriggeredTutorial(key)` appends a non-empty key once. Guides record when contraction starts, not while queued, and persist through normal saves. Older v1 saves without this field load an empty list; the version stays `1`.

`map` is an object keyed by player key. Every `playerKeys` entry must have exactly one non-empty normalised map path, and extra keys fail loading. `GameInstance:getCurrentMapPath()` returns the primary player's stored map or `nil`. `applyMapInfo` writes that same entry. `getVisitedMapPaths()` returns sorted telepoint map paths, and `getTelepointsForMap(key)` ignores the extension when matching. Both collection queries return copies. `restoreFromData(data)` restores a validated save into the instance.

`SAVE_AS_LDC` selects plain `.json` saves (`false`, the default) or compressed, obfuscated binary `.ldc` saves (`true`). **Encrypt save contents** sets the native default for C++ Source packages. Any project, including Standalone, can override it with the global assignment `SAVE_AS_LDC = true` or `false` at the top of `Scripts/Entry.lua`, before all `require` calls. `Source.Save` captures the format on first load, and later assignments have no effect.

`Source.Save` uses `Engine.saveData` and `Engine.loadData`; LDC is decoded directly into runtime data without JSON text. Old LDC saves containing compressed JSON are unsupported; changing `SAVE_AS_LDC` does not migrate them.

`GetSavePath(slot)` returns the save path for a 1-based slot number in the selected format.

Save previews load asynchronously without creating gameplay objects. Confirming a load calls `Save.LoadGame(filePath)` to restore the full game.

The window shows loading, empty or failed states. Each opening selects the most recently modified save, or the first slot if none exists. The selected slot receives keyboard focus after the opening animation.

New save screenshots preserve their aspect ratio and are no larger than 224 × 168 pixels. Existing larger screenshots remain readable.

Save encryption is independent of project JSON encryption, although Pack Options groups both under **Encrypt game data**.

## Native containers at data boundaries

Convert Standard `list`, `tuple` and `dict` values to Lua tables before saving them as JSON or LDC:

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
Engine.saveData("slot.ldc", payload:toTable())
```

Decoding either format yields ordinary Lua tables. Arrays include their logical length in `n`; root null and null array slots become nil, while null object fields retain `cjson.null`. Tuple-key strings, `cjson.null` nil slots and record-array reconstruction are in [Ludork Lua Advanced](<../../Getting Started/Ludork Lua Advanced.md>). Never persist an internal tuple hash.

## Limitations

Changing the save format does not rename or migrate existing slots. Choose the format before release, or provide a migration. Save upgrades, atomic writes, backups, cloud synchronisation and tuple-key record formats remain project responsibilities.

## Related pages

- [GlobalFunctions.Save](<../Node Functions/Save.md>)
- [Game Settings Reference](<Game Settings Reference.md>)
