## TabView

Direct metadata bases: `{ "Engine", "ControlBase" }`, `{ "Engine", "FunctionalBase" }`

### Selection and navigation

A TabView has a fixed, non-zero item count, zero-based clamped indices and an always-visible selection. The middle area contains equal tab slots, and each side reserves 16 logical pixels for hints. The control never takes keyboard focus. Declarative assets construct that fixed count from the required non-empty `items: string[]` property, and `tabCount` is not an asset property.

`setItems(items)` replaces same-count labels without changing the selection or the callback, while a wrong count leaves the control unchanged. `setOnSelectedIndexChanged(callback)` binds the selection callback, and `nil` clears it. A real `setSelectedIndex` change calls the callback without sound. `selectPrevious`, `selectNext` and real Q/E, LB/RB, mouse-move or touch-tap changes play the configured cursor sound once and then call the callback. Unchanged and boundary selections do neither, and tabs do not wrap.

Focused content calls `handleNavigationInput()`. It consumes Q, E, LB and RB while the TabView is visible and active. Duplicate same-direction inputs move once, and opposing inputs cancel. Mouse movement selects central slots. A left click there is consumed but does not select, while right and middle clicks and both hint gutters pass through. Touch movement does not select, but a tap does.

### Key hints

`setKeyHint(leftHint, rightHint)` accepts two `Engine.KeyHint` values with optional `Keyboard` and `Joystick` fields, which hold a non-Unknown `sf.Keyboard.Key` and an `Engine.JoystickButton` getter value respectively. An empty hint clears that side, and a missing current-device field hides it. Invalid input leaves both hints unchanged.

```lua
tabView:setKeyHint(
    Engine.KeyHint.new({ Keyboard = sf.Keyboard.Key.Q, Joystick = Engine.JoystickButton.getLB() }),
    Engine.KeyHint.new({ Keyboard = sf.Keyboard.Key.E, Joystick = Engine.JoystickButton.getRB() })
)
```

Hints appear only where movement is possible. A connected joystick uses the `Joystick` hint, otherwise desktop, HarmonyOS 2in1 and HarmonyOS Mobile tablets use `Keyboard`, while Android, iOS and HarmonyOS phones hide hints. Hints never rebind or disable input.

## GamepadHintBar

Direct metadata bases: `{ "Engine", "ControlBase" }`, `{ "Engine", "FunctionalBase" }`

GamepadHintBar shows up to three gamepad hints, centred in its size. It draws and reacts only while a gamepad is connected. Each hint is an `Engine.GamepadHint` with `Button` (an `Engine.JoystickButton` getter value), `LongPress` and `Text`. `setHints` rejects more than three. Default windows place it on the bottom border through the shared `WindowChrome` asset, and `WindowBase` binds its callbacks.

A short-press hint draws the current controller’s button glyph on a 16 logical-pixel white circle, then the text. A long-press hint adds a green clockwise sector that fills over one second. Holding the button fires `setOnHintTriggered` once with the zero-based index at the one-second mark; release resets progress. `setHintEnabled` greys a hint, stops its progress and blocks its trigger.

No editable properties are declared beyond `size` and the plain-text configuration.

## SectorShape

Direct metadata bases: `{ "sf", "Drawable" }`, `{ "sf", "Transformable" }`

SectorShape is a base graphic, not a UI control, so it is not in the palette. It fills a pie slice clockwise from 12 o'clock, with the angle clamped to 0–360 degrees. `GamepadHintBar` and `Button` use it for long-press progress.

## ProgressBar

Direct metadata bases: `{ "Engine", "ControlBase" }`

Progress ranges from 0 to 1; values outside that range are clamped and non-finite values become 0. The background covers the full control, and the fill reveals the corresponding left portion as progress increases, without compressing the whole fill image into the current width. Display scale and presentation opacity apply to both layers.

Each layer independently retains its `sf.Texture` resource. Passing `nil` to its texture setter clears the image and restores solid-colour rendering. Texture Rects use source pixels; `nil` selects the whole image. A layer's colour multiplies its image, so set it to white to preserve the original colours. Size and progress remain unchanged when images are replaced or cleared.

## Slider

Direct metadata bases: `{ "Engine", "ControlBase" }`, `{ "Engine", "FunctionalBase" }`

# GlobalCore: Map and Fog

## FogController

Construct `GlobalCore.FogController.new()` for each map session. The controller owns configuration; the shared renderer owns its GPU resources. The Game project creates and attaches one controller per `GameMap`, so configuring one map cannot overwrite another map's fog.

| Instance method | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `applyFromMapData` | `settings: Engine.MapFogSettings` | — |
| `applyWorldFromMapData` | `settings: Engine.MapFogSettings` | — |
| `setWorldRegionFog` | `key: string`, `cellRect: sf.IntRect`, `settings: Engine.MapFogSettings` | — |
| `removeWorldRegionFog` | `key: string` | — |
| `clearFog` | — | — |
| `getSettings` | — | `Engine.MapFogSettings` copy |
| `getWorldRegionSettings` | `key: string` | settings copy or `nil` |

The region methods and `applyWorldFromMapData` are runtime-only Lua APIs. `applyFromMapData` replaces the base configuration while retaining regions. `applyWorldFromMapData` starts a world configuration by clearing prior regions; `clearFog` clears both the base and regional configuration. There are no global `update` or `drawOverlay` calls. Map composition samples fog at the frame's absolute time, after material and light composition and before foreground weather and particles.

Fog uses GPU procedural noise in world coordinates. It needs no texture path. The base world fog is composed first; resident child fog is clipped to its placement and composed in stable placement order. Matching settings and time produce continuous noise across neighbouring placements. Lit fog samples the scene's ambient and direct light; Unlit uses its configured colour. See [Engine.MapFogSettings](<../Engine/Maps and Materials.md#mapfogsettings>) for fields and defaults.

## PanoramaController

### Functions and events

| Name | Kind | Parameters | Returns | Execution and metadata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `applyFromMapData` | `function` | mapData: { "GlobalCore", "MapPanoramaSettings" } | — | — |
| `clear` | `function` | — | — | — |
| `isActive` | `function` | — | return: bool | Pure |

`MapPanoramaSettings` accepts a Lua table with a `panorama` string. A missing or nil `panorama` defaults to `""`. Extra map fields are ignored. An invalid type raises an error. A blank `panorama` disables the underlay. `applyFromMapData` and `applyWorldFromMapData` share this configuration. A non-blank path loads the texture immediately, and a load failure propagates.

`getPath()` returns the current panorama path. Panorama rendering uses the shared compositor and keeps Cover scaling and Camera-dependent scrolling.

## PathResult

| Name | Type | Default | Metadata |

## GameMapBase

### Functions and events

| Name | Kind | Parameters | Returns | Execution and metadata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `generateDataFromMap` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; size: sf.Vector2u; materialMap: any[][]; smooth: bool | return: sf.Texture | — |
| `findPathExt` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; start: sf.Vector2i; goal: sf.Vector2i; size: sf.Vector2u; movingActor: { "Engine", "Actor" }; excludedAnchors: sf.Vector2i[] = {  } | return: { "GlobalCore", "PathResult" } | — |
| `getMaterialPropertyMapExt` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; width: int; height: int; propertyName: string; invalidValue: any | return: any[][] | — |
| `rebuildPassabilityCache` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; size: sf.Vector2u | return: bool[][] | — |
| `updateActorOccupancy` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; actor: { "Engine", "Actor" } | — | — |
| `getActorsAt` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; x: int; y: int | return: { "Engine", "Actor[]" } | — |
| `getActorsInRange` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; x: int; y: int; radius: int | return: { "Engine", "Actor[]" } | — |
| `getCollisionAt` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; x: int; y: int; selfActor: { "Engine", "Actor" } | return: { "Engine", "Actor[]" } | — |
| `getOverlapsAt` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; x: int; y: int; selfActor: { "Engine", "Actor" } | return: { "Engine", "Actor[]" } | — |
| `setTilemap` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; tilemap: { "Engine", "Tilemap" } | — | — |
| `syncActorsRef` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; actors: any | — | — |
| `setHideDisconnectedRegions` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; enabled: bool | — | — |
| `setVisibilityObserver` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; position: sf.Vector2i? = nil | — | — |
| `isCellVisible` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; position: sf.Vector2i | return: bool | Pure |
| `isActorVisibleOnMap` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self"; actor: { "Engine", "Actor" } | return: bool | Pure |
| `getVisibilityRevision` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "GameMapBase" } = "self" | return: int | Pure |

The runtime-only methods of `GameMapBase` (`metadata = false`) cover sparse-region readiness, the 1-based `getSparseWorldRegionIndexAt(position)`, region installation and removal.

### Region visibility

For ordinary finite maps, `setHideDisconnectedRegions(enabled)` enables or disables region hiding. `setVisibilityObserver(position)` accepts an `sf.Vector2i` cell for previews; passing `nil` resumes following the player. `isCellVisible(position)` queries the tile display mask, where impassable cells remain visible. `isActorVisibleOnMap(actor)` checks the Actor and each ancestor using their visibility flags and region rules: passable anchors use their region, while impassable anchors require the transformed image rectangle to overlap a visible passable cell. `getHideDisconnectedRegions()` is a runtime-only getter for the current switch. `getVisibilityRevision()` returns the current revision for display and preview caches, tracking terrain changes even while hiding is disabled. Visibility queries update pending changes before returning.

Changing terrain rebuilds connectivity and replacement sources. Moving within one region reuses the mask; moving to another region updates rendering and lighting. The renderer uses separate display layers, keeping the original tilemap intact. The selection rule and gameplay effects are documented in [Global.GameMap](<../../Global APIs/GameMap.md#disconnected-regions>).

## Shared map rendering

`GlobalCore.GameMapRenderer` adapts live map and Actor state to the Core `MapRenderer`; it does not own a second lighting algorithm. `drawContent` preserves the supplied render states and draws the ordered content. `composeFrame(ambientLight, time)` combines that Camera content with materials, lighting, panorama and fog. `prewarm(ambientLight, time)` warms the same rendering path. `setFogController(controller)` attaches the map's instance; `setLayerOrder(names)` follows world layer changes.

The Core renderer accepts scene, region, sprite, light and view records without Actor or Lua dependencies and retains its render targets and light caches between frames. Ordinary editor maps, world canvases and thumbnails use that same renderer through PreviewHost. Unlit uses white ambient with no direct light or shadows while preserving opacity, reflections, Actor/layer shaders and hue. Panorama and fog are independent display options. Lit uses the supplied ambient and Actor lights.

## Static preview rendering

`GlobalCore.PreviewSprite` and `GlobalCore.GameMapRenderer` are runtime-only Lua APIs (`metadata = false`), not Blueprint nodes. `PreviewSprite.new(table)` accepts these display fields:

| Fields | Meaning and defaults |
|---|---|
| `layer`, `texture`, `rect` | Layer name, retained `sf.Texture` or `nil`, and `sf.IntRect` source rectangle. |
| `position`, `mapPosition`, `translation` | Pixel anchor, region-visibility cell, and pixel display offset. |
| `rotation`, `scale`, `origin` | Degrees (default `0`), scale (default `{1, 1}`), and pixel origin. |
| `visible`, `parentIndex` | Own visibility (default `true`); zero-based earlier record index, or `-1` for a root. |
| `hue`, `shaderPath` | Hue in degrees (default `0`) and fragment shader path (default empty). |

`renderer:setPreviewSprites(records)` requires a renderer constructed with `previewOnly = true`. It retains the display resources and preserves record order within each configured layer. Parents must precede children; invalid parent indices fail without replacing the installed records. Explicitly installing an empty array draws no static sprites. Until records are installed, the renderer retains its ordinary Actor rendering contract.

`renderer:setPreviewVisibility(flags)` requires installed records and exactly one boolean per record, in the same order. It updates own visibility; effective visibility also includes ancestors and the map's region rules. A `nil` texture draws nothing but retains the record's geometry and parent role. Geometry is already resolved into map coordinates; `parentIndex` controls visibility, not transform composition.

Static shader drawing supports hue, uses `texture`, `textureSize`, `textureRect` and the supplied absolute `time` (`0` for floor previews), and combines sprite transforms with the caller's render states, including world offsets. A shader-load failure reports the error and draws the image in magenta. The native-only `GameMapBase::isSpriteVisibleOnMap(position, bounds, transform)` shares the geometry visibility test with live Actors; it is not a Lua binding.

## WorldStreamingState

`WorldRegionState` exposes `Unloaded`, `Reading`, `Prepared`, `Active` and `Dormant`. `WorldRegionDemand` exposes `None`, `Prepared` and `Active`. `WorldStreamingState` uses 1-based indices and owns the demand queues, Camera ordering, last-used and cache accounting, eviction and statistics. Camera ordering places Active regions first, then orders by squared centre distance and breaks ties by region index. The methods of `WorldStreamingState` are `metadata = false`. Blueprint uses contextual world-map nodes.

Lua calls `updateCameraCenter` and `updateDemand`, and consumes `takeReadBatch` and `takePublishItem`. Lua reports read and publish completion or cancellation, marks activation, deactivation and eviction, and reads `getEvictionList` and `getStats`. Files, builders and payloads remain Lua-owned.

## Light

`GlobalCore.Light.MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS` is a static, read-only `int` giving the compiled light limit shared by ordinary-map rendering and Lua world rendering. Its current value is `64`. Every visible light is a candidate: map lights and Actor lights draw on the same budget, and the renderer keeps the ones whose centres lie nearest the view centre, so a light is discarded only when more than that many are visible at once. Equal distances break by position, so the selection never depends on Actor iteration order. The source and rebuild rules are in [Build and Module Layout](<../../../../Native C++ Development/Build and Module Layout.md#shared-format-and-rendering-constants>).

# GlobalCore: Resource Managers

The generic managers require `/Game/Assets/...` paths with exact case, and they read both loose files and `.ldpak` archives. Native absolute paths, `Assets/...` paths and category-relative paths are invalid.

Archive compression is transparent to these APIs. Seekable streams decode one block at a time and report original file sizes and byte positions. Each loaded block is CRC32-checked; complete reads also check the file CRC32.

## AudioManager

Music, sound and voice switches and volumes are configured here. `set*` applies and saves, while `save*` only persists the value.

### Functions and events

# GlobalCore: Scenes and System

## SceneBase

Closing the window during runtime or input processing ends the current frame before further UI updates, emitter simulation or rendering. Closing it from an input or UI callback also skips the remaining frame work. The loop stops its logic thread and runs `onQuit` through the normal Scene exit lifecycle.

On Android and iOS, losing focus pauses scene and UI updates, rendering, runtime callbacks and scene timers while the loop continues processing system events. Returning to the foreground in the same process preserves the scene and Lua state, resets the frame and fixed-update timing, and resumes without catching up on time spent in the background. An actual close still follows the normal exit lifecycle.

### Scene timers

`scene:addTimer(interval, task, params, blocking)` returns an `Engine.AsyncOperation`. On expiry, it runs `task` before completing with `true` and resuming the Blueprint `TimeUp` branch. Callback errors propagate.

The Lua-only `scene:cancelTimers()` cancels unfinished timers and clears their input blocking. Calling it from a timer callback also cancels the current operation and skips any remaining callbacks. Scene exit or destruction cancels timers automatically.

### Functions and events

| Name | Kind | Parameters | Returns | Execution and metadata |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `getUIManager` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self" | return: { "GlobalCore", "UIManager" } | Pure |
| `addTimer` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self"; interval: float = nil; task: function = nil; params: any[] = {  }; blocking: bool = false | return: { "Engine", "AsyncOperation" } | Latent; LatentStates { [1] = "TimeUp", TimeUp = true } |
| `isInputBlocked` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self" | blocked: bool | Pure |
| `addAnim` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self"; anim: { "GlobalCore", "Animation" } | — | ExecSplit { [1] = "default", default = nil } |
| `getAnims` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self" | anims: { "GlobalCore", "Animation[]" } | Pure |
| `removeAnim` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self"; anim: { "GlobalCore", "Animation" } | — | ExecSplit { [1] = "default", default = nil } |
| `clearAnims` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self" | — | ExecSplit { [1] = "default", default = nil } |
| `addCommonTip` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self"; text: string | — | ExecSplit { [1] = "default", default = nil } |
| `onEnter` | `function` | self: { "GlobalCore", "SceneBase" } = "self" | — | — |

All runtime services below are static types under `GlobalCore`. Configuration keeps its existing INI keys and defaults; each service owns its values and apply/save behaviour.

## System

`GlobalCore.System` owns configuration startup, the main loop, runtime lifecycle and script/language settings. `System.run()` enters the loop from Lua and is excluded from Blueprint metadata.

### Functions and events

| Name | Kind | Parameters | Returns | Execution and metadata |

| `init` | `function` | data: ludork::standard::ConfigParser; dataFilePath: string | — | — |

| `exit` | `function` | — | — | — |

## Display

`GlobalCore.Display` owns the window, logical size, display scale, input method and presentation settings. `Display.initializeDisplay(title, gameSize, iconPath, cursorPath)` prepares the display from Lua and is excluded from Blueprint metadata.

### Display scale semantics

`getConfiguredScale()` returns the configured display preference, including `0`. `getScale()` returns the positive effective scale that rendering and input currently use after Maximum Render Scale is applied. The default configured preference is Fullscreen (`0`). `setScale` applies the value and saves it. `applyScale` only applies the value, and `saveScale` only saves it. Non-finite or negative values normalise to `1`. On desktop, `0` selects borderless fullscreen without changing the display mode. Positive values set a fixed standalone window size controlled through Scale, and users cannot drag its borders to resize it. Rendering preserves aspect ratio with centred black bars when needed. On macOS, the configured window scale is measured in Cocoa client points. The effective render scale returned by `getScale()` and `Engine.GetScale()` is calculated from the actual drawable pixel size, including the Retina backing scale, and then limited by Maximum Render Scale. A backing-scale change rebuilds the render targets and refreshes text without resizing the logical window.

`isDisplayScaleConfigurable()` is true for standalone desktop windows, including HarmonyOS 2in1, and false for embedded or ordinary mobile displays. In a HarmonyOS Mobile build for API 22 or newer, the result is true only on a tablet with free-window mode enabled. The ArkTS host listens for `freeWindowModeChange` and updates the native state. The runtime reapplies its current configured Scale when free-window mode is enabled and when the app returns to the foreground with that mode enabled. A positive value then requests a drawable client area of `round(gameSize * scale)` pixels; the host adds the window decorations to obtain the Stage's outer size. A value of `0` requests a maximised or fullscreen window. The host disables user drag resizing, so window size and fullscreen are controlled through Scale. Rendering uses the resulting surface and preserves aspect ratio with centred black bars if system size limits prevent the requested client size. HarmonyOS 2in1 follows the desktop scale protocol (default `0`).

`getMaximumWindowedScale(gameSize)` returns the largest scale that fits the available window dimensions. Desktop, including HarmonyOS 2in1, uses the decorated work area of the current window, or the primary display when no window exists. A configurable Mobile host supplies its own maximum and refreshes it when HarmonyOS free-window mode is enabled or the app returns to the foreground with that mode enabled. The result is `nil` for embedded and non-configurable mobile hosts, for zero logical dimensions and for unknown available sizes.

### Anti-aliasing semantics

Anti-aliasing defaults to `8`, and an invalid value uses the SFML default. `setAntiAliasingLevel` saves the value without recreating the current context, so the level applies at the next display initialisation. SFML may negotiate another supported level.

### Frame rate semantics

`getFrameRate()` returns the configured target, which defaults to `60`. A value of `0` means Unlimited and disables active frame-rate limiting. Vertical Sync remains independent and can still limit presentation. `setFrameRate` applies the value and saves it. `saveFrameRate` only saves. Fixed updates use a `1/60`-second step with Unlimited, or `1/framerate` for a positive target.

### iOS graphics context

On iOS, startup requires an OpenGL ES 3.0 or later context.

| `setInputMethodDisabled` | `function` | disabled: bool | — | — |

## Graphics

`GlobalCore.Graphics` owns the canvas, views, drawing and ordered shader chain, and coordinates frame composition and submission.

Graphics canvas textures use premultiplied alpha. Custom full-screen shaders must return premultiplied or opaque colours.

### Maximum render scale semantics

`getMaximumRenderScale()` returns the cap on the effective physical-pixel render scale. A value of `0` means unlimited, the default is `2`, and an invalid value also becomes `2`. `setMaximumRenderScale` applies the value and saves it between frames without resizing the window. `saveMaximumRenderScale` only saves. For a `640×480` game at configured scale `1.5` on a Retina 2× display, the window is `960×720` Cocoa points: an unlimited cap renders at `1920×1440` (effective scale `3`), while a cap of `2` renders at `1280×960` in the same window.

### Lighting render scale semantics

`getLightingRenderScale()` returns `0.5`, `0.75` or `1`. The default is `1`, also used for invalid values. `setLightingRenderScale` applies the value and saves it, rebuilding direct-light targets and invalidating the static cache. `saveLightingRenderScale` only saves. The surface mask, transmission and occupancy remain at full resolution.

## ScreenEffects

`GlobalCore.ScreenEffects` owns flash, shake and screen tone, including their active/completion queries.

## Transition

`GlobalCore.Transition` owns transition requests and frozen backgrounds. `requestTransition` accepts an empty optional value or a complete `/Game/Assets/Transitions/...` logical path without adding a prefix. Freeze requests complete when the outgoing frame has been captured; transition completion is confirmed after the final frame has been submitted.

`setTransition`, `freezeTransitionBackground` and `requestTransition` return `Engine.AsyncOperation` with a successful result of `true`. For Blueprint `Frozen` / `Finished` branches, use the [Transition nodes](<../../../Node Functions/Transition.md>).

A new request of the same kind cancels the previous unfinished operation. `cancelTransitionBackgroundFreeze()` cancels the freeze operation and clears the frozen state. `cancelPendingTransition()` cancels only a not-yet-applied request, leaving an already-running transition intact. Runtime reset or shutdown cancels remaining operations.

`GlobalCore.SceneManager` owns the current scene, scene stack and queued switches. It preserves the scene-thread and deferred-destruction lifecycle. Request application exit through `System.exit()`.

## RuntimeDiagnostics

`RuntimeDiagnostics.isPerformanceProfilerEnabled()` queries whether profiling is enabled. `recordWorldStreamingPerformance(queueDepth, reading, prepared, active, dormant, cacheBytes, publishMilliseconds, visibleTileChunks, activeActors)` records a streaming sample. Both methods are available to Lua and excluded from Blueprint metadata.

Weather and panorama use `WeatherController` and `PanoramaController`. Each `GameMap` owns its own `FogController`; use `gameMap:getFogSettings()` and `gameMap:setFogSettings(settings)` for that map. The shared map compositor renders its fog before foreground weather and particles; see [Map and Fog](<Map and Fog.md>). Audio switches and volumes belong to [AudioManager](<Resource Managers.md#audiomanager>).

# GlobalCore: UI, Weather and Module Root

## UIManager

### Stacking and update order

`UIManager` renders and late-updates in ascending `Canvas.zOrder`, but runs logic and fixed updates in reverse order, so that foreground UIs consume input first. At equal z-order, the later-loaded UI is in front.

# GlobalFunctions Lua API

`GlobalFunctions` exposes native free functions through the `Components`, `Manager`, `NodeGraph` and `UI` group tables. The declarations come from `Scripts/stub/GlobalFunctions.d.lua` and `Engine/Source/GlobalFunctions/include/GlobalFunctions`. `Scripts/GlobalFunctions_meta.lua` is empty, so these functions are Lua APIs rather than Blueprint nodes. A grouped function appears only in its group table.

Lua Blueprint functions in `Scripts/GlobalFunctions` load as separate modules, such as `require("GlobalFunctions.Math")`. They are not added to this native root table.

## Loading

See [Lua Runtime and Modules](<../../Lua Runtime and Modules.md#entry-and-module-order>) for module loading order.

## Components

The component utilities in this group support class metadata, serialisation and attachment. Names beginning with `_` and functions declared `metadata = false` are runtime infrastructure, so project gameplay uses the public class and component workflow instead.

`getComponentFieldValue` and `setComponentFieldValue` require the declared component instance. A missing or wrong-type component raises instead of being rebuilt.

| `getFontFilenameList` | — | string[] |

| `loadTexture` | subFolder: string; filename: string; sRGB: bool = false; area: sf.IntRect = nil; smooth: bool = false | sf.Texture |

| `loadShader` | shaderPath: string; shaderType: sf.Shader.Type = nil | sf.Shader |
| `loadFullShaderWithGeo` | vertPath: string; geoPath: string; fragPath: string | sf.Shader |
| `loadGeoShader` | vertPath: string; geoPath: string; fragPath: string | sf.Shader |

## NodeGraph

| Name | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `initLatent` | — | — | Initialises latent-node support; runtime infrastructure with `metadata = false`. |

## UI

`HexColor` is overloaded for a hexadecimal string or a packed integer. Both overloads use `alpha = 255` when the input does not supply an alpha value.

| Name | Parameters | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `HexColor` | value: string; alpha: int = 255 | sf.Color |
| `HexColor` | value: int; alpha: int = 255 | sf.Color |
| `GetRosyBrown` | — | sf.Color |

| `GetSteelBlue` | — | sf.Color |
| `GetDimGrey` | — | sf.Color |
| `GetCharcoal` | — | sf.Color |

## Limitations

Category helpers accept only category-relative paths and add their `/Game/Assets/...` prefix, as in `loadCharacter("actors/Hero.png")` and `playSE("cursor.ogg")`. Stored data and `getSoundBuffer(filePath)` require complete logical paths instead. Loading failures follow the native manager contract.

documents.content:
# Build and Module Layout

Choose a C++ Source project when the Lua and Blueprint APIs are insufficient, when a new native UI adapter is required, or when producing an iOS, HarmonyOS or Android build. The runtime uses C++20, CMake and declaration-driven bindings.

Choose the correct native module, build its generated bindings and load the resulting Lua modules in the supported order.

## Prerequisites

- A C++ Source project with CMake, a C++20 toolchain and its platform dependencies installed.
- A clean build configuration for the target platform.
- A supported target: Windows 10 or newer on x64, macOS 13.3 or newer on Apple Silicon, iOS 16.3 or newer on arm64, HarmonyOS 6.0.2 / API 22 or newer on arm64-v8a, or Android 7.0 / API 24 or newer on arm64-v8a.

Public headers contain ordinary C++ declarations plus `BIND_*` markers that expand to nothing at compile time. Core bindgen reads the module and shared Runtime declaration roots, then generates one stable LuaGlue source per class, one module aggregate and stub source, a LuaLS stub and editor metadata.

The `LUDORK_OPTIMIZE_DEBUG` setting also controls Debug interprocedural optimisation for LuaSF binding objects and the shared LuaGlue runtime.

Windows MSVC Release builds use deterministic compilation and `/Brepro` linking with incremental linking disabled, including the SFML and Lua dependencies. The separate FFmpeg build uses the same linker policy. This removes build-time timestamp differences from rebuilt EXE/DLL files when updating a Standalone project's `Binaries`. The first rebuild with these settings changes existing binaries once; changes to native inputs, dependencies, compiler, SDK or build settings can still change their contents. Packages continue to omit PDB files; retain the matching build symbols for debugging.

## Steps

Enable the optional [`GlobalCore.Server` API](<../Simple Server/Native Client API.md>) through the [server build settings](<../Simple Server/Deployment and Editor Settings.md>). Changing its development URL or key requires a Debug rebuild. When disabled, the Lua API remains callable and returns `ServerErrorCode.Disabled`.

### Choose a module

| Module | Responsibility | Native dependency direction |
|---|---|---|
| `LudorkRuntime` | Values, VM/binding services, Blueprint execution, typed/component data, JSON and Asset/Data/Script stores, GPU particle simulation and drawing | Standard, SFML and private zlib, plus LuaSF in full mode; never Core modules |
| `Engine` | Engine types, services, state and gameplay foundations | LudorkRuntime and SFML |
| `GlobalCore` | Global game classes and services | Engine, Standard, SFML and LudorkVideo; optional platform libraries |
| `GlobalFunctions` | `Components`, `UI`, `NodeGraph` and `Manager` free-function groups | GlobalCore and SFML |
| `LudorkVideo` | Shared video decoding, seeking and audio extraction under `Engine/Source/Media` | LudorkRuntime, SFML and FFmpeg when enabled |

`LudorkVideo` (`Ludork::Video`) is a static library for video playback. It exposes no Lua root.

`LudorkRuntime` is shared on desktop and static on mobile, and it exposes no Lua root. Bindings remain under `Engine`. AssetStore, DataStore and ScriptStore define the read-only Asset, Data and Lua-module boundaries for both the loose layout and the `.ldpak` layout. Standard receives DataStore file access only, so script archives never appear through filesystem APIs. Private zlib handles archive decompression and CRC32. Gameplay modules keep a fixed load order, do not link back to `GlobalFunctions` and carry complete cross-module declarations.

`.ldpak` v1 is little-endian. Its `LDPK` header stores the version, group, entry count, index range and CRC32. The file and directory index is sorted by UTF-8 byte order and records paths, directory flags, 64-bit data offsets, original and stored sizes, file CRC32 and block counts. Each path is followed by its block descriptors: stored size, compression flag and original-data CRC32. File data starts on an 8-byte boundary; blocks follow consecutively, with original sizes derived from the 1 MiB block size and file size. Empty files have no blocks. The writer uses an independent zlib level-6 stream per block only when it is smaller than the original.

Archive and stream readers share block decoding. Each stream caches only its current decoded block, seeks in original bytes and validates block CRC32 on loading; complete reads also validate the file CRC32. Invalid block ranges, lengths, truncated or trailing compressed data and checksum failures are rejected. Streams return their existing failure result; complete-file reads throw an error.

Runtime owns Blueprint class generation, Script Mixins, graph execution and latent scheduling. Engine supplies Actor graph lookup, EventBus and frame-loop integration. `RuntimeProviders.installBlueprint(classDataByPath, compileGraph, instantiateGraphTemplate)` installs its three Blueprint callbacks. ClassDict delegates to the VM resolver. Cache and definition identity follow the rules in [Execution Flow, Events and Variables](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Blueprint Scripting/Execution Flow Events and Variables.md#class-definitions-and-session-lifetime>).

The C++ `BlueprintRuntimeFacade::hasEvents(objects, eventNames)` returns an object-by-event boolean matrix. Actor update batches use it to reuse class event checks within one synchronisation. Instance graphs and own methods are checked separately, and the class cache ends with the call, so later synchronisations observe method and graph changes. Actors whose ticks are disabled defer event checks until ticks become enabled; their event mask is then resolved after the native update and before event dispatch, and retained until the next synchronisation. Native updates still run for every Actor.

Engine owns the `RuntimeProviders` binding facade. Its data resolvers retain typed Curve and PlainTextConfig callbacks in Core, while Blueprint and config installation delegates to Runtime. Fixed-signature providers validate one result at the call boundary; Graph results use shared native ownership. Runtime does not include Core data types. Missing or duplicate installations, wrong results and stopped sessions remain errors.

Bootstrap-only native modules are host-owned. The application registers `cjson` and `cjson.safe`, Standard owns `Class` registration, and Engine uses its initialised native tables and APIs instead of reverse module links. Dynamic module resolution remains driven by assets and metadata.

`LUDORK_SAVE_AS_LDC` is a CMake option that defaults to `OFF`. Standard exposes it as `SAVE_AS_LDC` before Entry runs. C++ Source packaging sets this default through **Encrypt save contents**. Entry overrides follow the rules in [Runtime Data, Configuration and Saves](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Default Gameplay/Runtime Data Configuration and Saves.md#saves>).

The game application host lives in `Application/` (`include/` and `src/`). Android and HarmonyOS application shells live under `Engine/PlatformHosts/Android` and `Engine/PlatformHosts/Harmony`. Build support lives in `Engine/cmake/`, including the FFmpeg builds in `Engine/cmake/FFmpeg/`.

`runtimeWindowStyle()` in `GlobalRuntime.cpp` defines the game window style once. Its fixed-window policy flows to SFML window creation and recreation, native work-area measurements and the HarmonyOS ArkTS host. Platform adapters translate the supplied style into window controls and frame dimensions; they do not choose a separate resize policy. Display Scale and fullscreen remain runtime settings.

`LUDORK_WITH_LUA` defaults to `ON` and is required for game builds.

Game builds generate native bindings and validate UI assets through the project registry. UI Lua Views and declarations are generated separately by editor **Export** or explicit `ScriptTools ui-assets generate <project-root>`; builds do not generate them. The UI generator itself needs no desktop preview. The [Declarative UI Authoring Workflow](<../Lua and Blueprint Scripting/Declarative UI/Authoring Workflow.md>) describes generated and handwritten ownership.

Source preview and game binaries share `bin/<configuration>`. Desktop builds generate the [project preview artefacts](<Native UI Adapters.md#project-preview-artefacts>). Mobile cross-builds use an explicitly supplied desktop registry.

### Shared map rendering and preview boundary

`Engine/Source/Core/include/Graphics/MapRenderer.hpp` defines the common native map renderer. Engine and PreviewHostRuntime compile the same Core Graphics implementation. `Scene` contains ordered layers, placed tilemap regions, resolved sprite appearances, component lights, ambient light, panorama and fog. `View` and `Options` carry the camera, output dimensions, time and display options. The result is an `sf::RenderTexture`; the renderer does not parse editor requests or read pixels back to the CPU.

Ordinary maps use one region. Worlds draw regions within each authoritative layer, preserving placement priority and cross-region lighting and occlusion. `GlobalCore.GameMapRenderer` adapts gameplay state and supplies emitter, billboard, layer-effect and ordinary-map player-cover hooks. Native `TileLayer::updateBlock` rebuilds affected chunks and autotile neighbours and invalidates material and occlusion caches. Streaming retains `writeBlock` and its normal build stages. Animation uses the explicit frame time.

`Engine/PreviewHost` owns request parsing, editor sessions, process communication, BGRA readback and temporary frame transport, outside Core's recursive source collection. The editor sends resolved visual records without running Actor creation, Tick or Blueprint gameplay events. A full scene initialises a session; subsequent changes update scene fields and regions, while camera and animation requests reuse the installed scene. Game modules neither include this implementation nor link its dedicated runtime library. `LudorkRuntime` keeps its downward dependency boundary without depending on map gameplay objects.

A preview-only CMake build enables `LUDORK_BUILD_PREVIEW_HOST` and disables `LUDORK_BUILD_GAME_APPLICATION`. A game-only build disables the preview switch and supplies `LUDORK_UI_REGISTRY_PATH` with a matching desktop UI registry for asset validation. Full desktop development builds enable both targets. See [project preview artefacts](<Native UI Adapters.md#project-preview-artefacts>) for tools and packaging rules.

### Shared format and rendering constants

`ScriptTools/runtime_formats.py` owns the `.ldpak` and encrypted-payload layouts, versions, binary data tags and codec limits; `ScriptTools/resource_constants.py` owns resource groups, paths and suffixes. CMake runs `ScriptTools runtime-constants cpp <project-root> <output-directory>` to generate neutral C++ headers under `Intermediate/<build-name>-<hash>/RuntimeConstants/LudorkGenerated`. Native consumers link `Ludork::RuntimeConstants`; implementation layers never include a parent host's private headers to obtain these values. Engine exposes the four data and animation suffixes through `ResourceFileConstants`.

`Assets/Shaders/Global/UnoccludedLightPass.frag` contains the sole `LUDORK_MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS` definition: one decimal integer in `1..256`, currently `64`. Generation rejects missing, repeated or invalid definitions. Changing this limit requires rebuilding the native project so the shader, native renderer and read-only `GlobalCore.Light.MAX_SHADER_LIGHTS` agree. Ordinary shader reload alone does not update the compiled limit.

Generation runs for game, desktop Preview and `LUDORK_WITH_LUA=OFF` builds. C++ Source templates retain the shader source and build wiring; their normal build regenerates the headers. Generated headers are build outputs and are not edited or shipped as template sources.

### LDC binary data

`Runtime/Data.hpp` owns `loadData`, `saveData`, `dataExists`, `decodeData` and the binary payload reader `parseBinaryData`; file APIs accept `std::filesystem::path` or UTF-8 strings. Lua exposes the four data-file APIs on `Engine`; `parseBinaryData` is a C++ payload-level API. `Runtime/Json.hpp` retains exact-path JSON text operations. Standard owns file access, path resolution and payload compression/obfuscation; it does not depend on Runtime or interpret the binary value tree.

LDC retains the `LDDC` envelope, version `1`, zlib compression, stream obfuscation and checksum. Source length and checksum describe the uncompressed binary payload. A one-byte tag precedes each value:

| Tag | Value and payload |
|---|---|
| `0`, `1`, `2` | Null, false and true, with no following payload. |
| `3` | Little-endian signed 64-bit integer. |
| `4` | Little-endian finite IEEE 754 binary64 number. |
| `5` | Little-endian uint32 byte length, followed by string bytes. |
| `6` | Little-endian uint32 count, followed by tagged array values. |
| `7` | Little-endian uint32 count, followed by string keys and tagged values. Keys use the string length/bytes encoding without a tag and are written in UTF-8 byte order. |

Empty arrays and maps remain distinct. The decoded payload is limited to 512 MiB and nesting to 256. Invalid tags, truncation, invalid lengths, duplicate keys, non-finite numbers and trailing bytes fail decoding. Functions, objects, cycles and reference restoration are outside this pure-data format. Old LDC payloads containing JSON text are rejected without fallback or migration; regenerate them from source data. Shader payloads keep their separate format.

### GPU particle ownership

Core keeps the public `Emitter`, `EmitterComponent`, `EmitterView` and Scene scheduling interfaces. Its `EmitterConfiguration` contains `EmitterTrack` values, each combining Runtime's `EmitterTrackParameters` with Core's eight named `EmitterCurves` channels of `Curve::CurveData`. `setConfiguration` centrally validates these values, samples the existing `Curve` implementation into a 256 × 8 float lookup table per track and restarts playback. `Runtime/Graphics/GpuEmitterCurveLayout.hpp` owns this layout: 256 samples across eight channels, packed into two RGBA rows. CPU baking, GPU texture allocation and generated shader coordinates use the same sample counts and indexing. `getConfiguration` returns an independent value copy. The existing ParticleSystem remains in Core.

Within the Emitter path, `RuntimeData` is confined to resource JSON input in Core's `EmitterResource.hpp/.cpp`. The resource adapter maps authored string choices, 0–255 colours, arrays and curve references to the fixed configuration fields. Emitter stores that configuration value; the backend stores its compiled configuration.

`Runtime/Graphics/GpuEmitterConfiguration.hpp` carries Runtime track parameters and baked curve samples without Core types. The unbound `GpuEmitterBackend` in `Runtime/Graphics/GpuEmitterBackend.hpp` owns playback state, fixed simulation steps, GPU tracks, drawing, asynchronous statistics and deferred GPU release through a private implementation. It accepts resolved configuration and does not interpret `Data/Particles` keys or depend on Core Curve, Actor or UI classes. `EmitterStatistics` is a Runtime value record with required `capacity`/`time` and optional renderer, count and timing results. Core returns it directly; the Lua binding writes a declared-field snapshot table, preserving unavailable optional values as `nil`.

The public Core `Emitter` forwards playback operations to this backend. Configuration, track, curves, burst and statistics records keep separate class-named headers, and their Lua registrations and declarations are generated through the normal binding build under `Engine`. Runtime has no additional Lua root.

GPU implementation files live under `Runtime/src/Graphics/Emitters`. Raw OpenGL functions, shaders, buffer/query identifiers and private GPU headers stay there. Texture reads reuse Runtime AssetStore and AssetInputStream, including the existing loose and packed layouts. Runtime depends on Standard and SFML; Core includes only Runtime's public graphics headers.

The Runtime Graphics CMake subdirectory compiles this backend once in both full and `LUDORK_WITH_LUA=OFF` builds.

Shared GPU resources are keyed by the active SFML context ID. Shutdown queues GPU objects without requiring a context on the caller's thread; collection runs with the matching resource context active. Scene and preview hosts retain ownership of windows/render targets and collect retired resources before destroying those contexts. This GPU lifetime is independent of the Lua VM lifetime.

### Session and module lifetime

Standard owns the Lua session. `runtime::initialize` requires a running Standard session, and repeated calls preserve the attached Runtime state. After `runtime::shutdown` detaches Runtime, a restart requires a new Standard session and Lua VM.

Standard shuts down modules in reverse dependency order (Global, Engine, Runtime) before releasing its state. The host owns the Lua VM, and it must wait for shutdown to finish on the thread that initiated it before calling `lua_close`. If LuaSF initialisation or binding registration fails before Standard starts, the host must still call `LuaSF_quiesce_state` and `LuaSF_shutdown_state` before `lua_close` to release any partially initialised glue session.

AssetStore, DataStore, ScriptStore and the Standard read-only file provider are host configuration. They are independent of the VM session and survive session shutdown.

Standard establishes a LuaGlue execution scope at each host Lua entry. Nested glue operations may reuse that scope only while the host confirms that the current thread still owns the VM lock and the execution hooks are unchanged. `LuaExecutionPause` suspends that ownership; operations during a pause must acquire the lock again. Hosts without an ownership probe continue to use the ordinary enter/leave hooks.

### Host and implementation sources

Each independent class or bound type uses a same-named header and, where needed, a source file. Public declarations belong under `include`, and member definitions under `src`. Owner-specific data types may be nested. Shared data and helper collections may stay together.

Host-private implementation stays under `src` and uses an `Impl` suffix, such as `HostImpl.hpp` for `Host::Impl`. Larger implementations may use a same-named subdirectory and contribute sources through `target_sources`. Dependencies flow from the host into its implementation. Child directories must not include parent-private headers, including through include-root shortcuts, and public headers must not include private headers.

Core shares SpriteVisuals, joystick device tracking and text configuration codecs through `src/Shared/include/CoreShared`. Their implementation and state remain under `src/Shared/src`; consumers include only the interface headers. Host companion headers stay beside their host source and are not shared interfaces.

Shared Runtime Lua services live in `Runtime/src/LuaServices`. Pure ConfigVars parsing lives in `Runtime/src/Metadata`.

Standard ClassRuntime dependencies flow `Class → Composite → Instance → Native → Detail`, with downward shortcuts allowed. Each layer owns a distinct concern:

- Detail owns neutral state and queries.
- Native owns native members and properties.
- Instance owns native construction and disposal.
- Composite owns indexing and metatables.
- Class coordinates allocation, finalisation and super.

The boundary checker includes Standard and rejects upward layer includes, parent-private includes and cycles formed by those edges.

System privately composes Display, FramePipeline, SceneStack and Lifecycle. Display owns the window. FramePipeline owns the canvas, effects and transition targets. SceneStack owns queued operations and retired scenes. Lifecycle owns shutdown state. Components expose operations instead of mutable state aggregates. Frame presentation remains outside the scene logic lock, and render targets rebuild between frames.

Each Scene logic worker creates and releases its own shared graphics context on that thread. The context stays alive throughout the logic loop, so rebuilding a Camera render texture on the render thread cannot destroy the logic worker's active context. The scene logic lock continues to serialise access to shared render textures.

`EngineState::CellSize` is a positive C++ compile-time constant. Changing it requires a rebuild of the engine, the editor and the templates. There is no project-level or runtime override.

### Native text input boundary

Engine owns the edit session through `Input/TextInputService.hpp`. Platform hosts implement `Input/TextInputHost.hpp`. The contract uses UTF-8, byte offsets at grapheme boundaries and caret rectangles in window-client pixels. Hosts return session-tagged events through a thread-safe sink. Service operations run on the game thread or before it starts. Standard provides Unicode segmentation and whitespace handling through utf8proc.

### Native WebView boundary

Runtime owns the native web-page service and the `Engine.OpenWebView(url)` binding. `Runtime/WebViewHost.hpp` defines the platform host factory, window attachment and session-tagged completion; `Runtime/WebViewService.hpp` supplies input blocking. Factories can be installed before VM initialisation. Display attaches a host to the live native window and detaches it before replacement or destruction. Each open request has a new ID; the host navigates its existing layer, and a late completion for an older request cannot close the current session. A rejected request preserves the existing page and session.

Platform hosts run UI work asynchronously and do not wait in the game loop or call Lua from completion. macOS and iOS use WKWebView, Android the system WebView, HarmonyOS ArkWeb, and Windows the system Evergreen WebView2 Runtime.

The HarmonyOS overlay root uses `HitTestMode.BLOCK_HIERARCHY`: its Web and Close button receive touch events, while lower siblings and ancestors do not. The game XComponent stays mounted beneath the overlay.

### Core headers and Runtime boundary

Core Lua-binding headers include `<CoreMinimal.hpp>` from `Engine/Runtime/include`. That header supplies annotations, runtime types, common C++ types and the SFML Graphics, Window and System modules. Include module exports and direct type dependencies explicitly. Every public header must compile independently.

Handwritten Core, including private sources, reaches VM and binding services through Runtime without direct or transitive LuaGlue dependencies. Runtime also owns isolated audio execution, while Core retains gameplay and playback policy. Generated bindings may use LuaGlue. Runtime internals use private operations within an active `RuntimeScope`. Facades provide the external entry boundary.

Choose API types, container ownership and Lua-reference operations using [Runtime Value Boundaries](<Runtime Value Boundaries.md>).

### Native pointer casts

`<CoreMinimal.hpp>` includes `<Cast.hpp>`; lower-level headers may include it directly. Use `ludork::Cast<T>(pointer)` for checked native downcasts and cross-casts after [declaring the cast protocol](<Macro Reference.md#native-cast-declarations>). `T` is the target class, without `*`. Known upcasts may use implicit conversion or `static_cast`; unchecked `static_cast` must not replace a dynamic type check.

Raw and shared pointers are supported. Null or mismatched inputs return empty results; constness and multiple-inheritance subobject offsets are preserved. Successful shared-pointer casts alias the original control block, and the rvalue overload transfers ownership only on success. There is no reference or `void` target overload.

Queries and dynamic type identification compare compiler-generated type-signature strings by content across modules. These keys are internal to a complete build with the same toolchain, not persistent IDs or a cross-toolchain ABI.

### Build the project

```bash
./tools/build_cpp.sh Game Debug
./tools/build_cpp.sh Game Release
```

```text
tools\build_cpp.bat Game Debug
tools\build_cpp.bat Game Release
```

In the editor, **Construct** runs the Debug build for a C++ Source project. After a direct CMake build, run an incremental `build_cpp` to update the build record used by **Play**. Changes to third-party sources or external CMake settings also require **Construct** or `build_cpp`. See [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>) for the editor workflow.

`LUDORK_OPTIMIZE_DEBUG` defaults to `ON` and controls Debug optimisation. LuaGlue checks argument types and bounds in every configuration.

First-party C++ must not use `dynamic_cast`, `std::dynamic_pointer_cast` or `typeid`. `Engine/cmake/LudorkCppOptions.cmake` disables RTTI for C++ and Objective-C++ in every configuration with `/GR-` on MSVC and `-fno-rtti` on GCC, Clang and AppleClang. This covers game, Preview, Lua-disabled builds, source-built dependencies. LuaGlue identifies types without RTTI; exception handling stays enabled. Rebuild all native modules together after changing this policy. Imported libraries and system frameworks retain their own settings.

Release builds enable IPO/LTO for Standard, its separate ClassRuntime OBJECT target and the final mobile application target, alongside Runtime and Core. MinGW keeps IPO disabled. ClassRuntime uses hidden symbols and hidden inline symbols, while explicit public exports remain available. On Apple platforms, the game application, Standard, Runtime and Core use `-dead_strip` for their final Release links. MSVC keeps separate PDB files and `/OPT:REF /OPT:ICF`; Android and HarmonyOS use their toolchain's section garbage collection. These Release settings do not change Debug optimisation or the public Lua API. Keep the matching unstripped build outputs and any generated debug-symbol files for diagnosing a release; [packaging](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md#packaging>) strips only the platform's final distribution output.

On macOS, single-arm64 AppleClang Release builds compile the generated Core binding sources with `-Os`. Handwritten runtime sources and other platforms, architectures and configurations retain their existing optimisation levels.

LuaSF is a binder only: it owns neither the Lua VM nor its dependencies. The game runtime creates the `lua_State` with `luaL_newstate` and `luaL_openlibs`, hands it to LuaSF with `LuaSF_initialize_state` and `LuaSF_register`, and tears it down through `ludork::standard::shutdown` and `lua_close`.

CMake reads LuaSF, LuaGlue, SFML and Lua from their directories under `Game/Engine/ThirdParty`. Override them with `-DLUDORK_LUASF_SOURCE_DIR`, `-DLUDORK_LUAGLUE_SOURCE_DIR`, `-DLUDORK_SFML_SOURCE_DIR` and `-DLUDORK_LUA_SOURCE_DIR`. LuaGlue defaults to the sibling of the selected LuaSF source directory, so local generator integration uses `-DLUDORK_LUASF_SOURCE_DIR=/path/to/LuaSF-AutoGenerator/output/LuaSF`. Dependency initialisation installs the two projects from one source archive and writes matching `.ludork-version` markers.

SFML is a required source project rather than an optional override, and LuaSF reuses the `sfml-*` targets Ludork builds from it. Mobile uses static SFML; desktop follows `LUASF_BUILD_SHARED_SFML`, defaulting to shared. `versions.conf` selects the SFML variant by repository and tag; the current pin is the SFML-ME `310-ME-OH-GLESVER` tag. OHOS GPU particles require an SFML source that preserves the GLES 3 context request; see [Common Particles](<../Editor User Guide/Common Particles.md>).

Local source archives can be selected with `LUASF_SOURCE_ARCHIVE` before dependency initialisation: use a `.tar.gz` with the shell entry point or a `.zip` on Windows. The archive must extract directly to `LuaSF/` and `LuaGlue/`; older source layouts are rejected. Both projects consume one Lua 5.5 runtime. Desktop builds share LuaGlue; mobile targets link it statically.

CMake runs `ScriptTools core-bindgen` automatically. See [Generated Metadata and Stubs](<Generated Metadata and Stubs.md>) for output locations, enum modules and cross-build requirements.

`Intermediate/` is excluded from templates and recreated by a normal build when missing. `bin/` and `build/` remain at the project root.

iOS uses a single-window `UIScene` host. The application scene manifest selects its scene delegate. The host associates its window with a `UIWindowScene` and starts the runtime once that scene is active. A temporary scene disconnection pauses the live runtime and retains its window for reconnection within the same session. This supports SDKs that require the scene lifecycle while the application and optional FFmpeg build retain an iOS 16.3 deployment target.

HarmonyOS packaging is an Apple Silicon macOS cross-build through DevEco Studio's OpenHarmony native SDK. Each package recreates its Stage and native build directories, so a CMake cache cannot cross device forms or graphics backends. The HAP target and the compatible SDK are both `6.0.2(22)`, and CMake receives `OHOS_COMPATIBLE_SDK_VERSION=22`. The toolchain therefore compiles Ludork, Lua, LuaSF, LuaGlue and SFML for `aarch64-linux-ohos22.0.0` with API availability diagnostics enabled. A newer installed SDK serves as the compile SDK only and does not raise that deployment target.

The Mobile variant configures `SFML_HARMONY_DEVICE_FORM=MOBILE` and `SFML_OPENGL_ES=ON`, advertises `phone` and `tablet`, and uses the fixed-landscape mobile host. The 2in1 variants configure `SFML_HARMONY_DEVICE_FORM=2IN1` and advertise only `2in1`. They support `fullscreen` and `floating` windows, publish `NEED_OPENGL=1`, request `ohos.permission.LOCK_WINDOW_CURSOR`, and set `SFML_OPENGL_ES=OFF` for OpenGL or `ON` for OpenGL ES. An FFmpeg-enabled HarmonyOS build keeps the same versioned compiler target for C and C++ compilation and linking, while retaining the OpenHarmony sysroot, MUSL selection and availability checks.

A 2in1 OpenGL binary has a hard dependency on `libGLv4.so`. If the image lacks that library, the dynamic loader rejects the NAPI module before native initialisation. The binary does not switch to OpenGL ES.

Android packaging is a cross-build from Apple Silicon macOS. The packer invokes host CMake 3.28 or newer with `Unix Makefiles`, the highest complete stable NDK r27-or-newer toolchain found under the local SDK's `ndk` directory, `ANDROID_PLATFORM=android-24`, `ANDROID_ABI=arm64-v8a` and `ANDROID_STL=c++_static`. The project never contains its own SDK or NDK. Lua, LuaSF, LuaGlue, Runtime, Core, cjson, SFML and optional FFmpeg targets are static. The only shared output is `libludork.so`, which Gradle consumes as a prebuilt `jniLibs` entry. Android Studio's SDK CMake and Ninja are not used.

### Load the runtime modules

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
local GlobalCore = require("GlobalCore")
local GlobalFunctions = require("GlobalFunctions")

local Components = GlobalFunctions.Components
local UI = GlobalFunctions.UI
local NodeGraph = GlobalFunctions.NodeGraph
local Manager = GlobalFunctions.Manager
```

Load these three roots in the displayed order. `GlobalFunctions` groups are accessed through their tables and must not leak into the module root. Standard globals are already installed. `CoreSystem` is not a runtime module.

## Related pages

- [Binding a Class](<Binding a Class.md>)
- [Functions, Events and Execution](<Functions Events and Execution.md>)
- [Runtime Value Boundaries](<Runtime Value Boundaries.md>)
- [Run, Debug and Package](<../Editor User Guide/Run Debug and Package.md>)

documents.content:
# Binding a Class

Expose one C++20 class consistently to native Lua, LuaLS and the Blueprint metadata catalogue.

## Prerequisites

- The owning module and dependency direction are already selected.
- The class has a public header and implementation under that module.

## Steps

### Declare the class

```cpp
#pragma once
#include <CoreMinimal.hpp>

BIND_CLASS()
class Counter {
public:
  BIND_INIT()
  explicit Counter(int initial = 0);

  BIND_PROPERTY()
  int value = 0;

  BIND_METHOD(Pure = true)
  int getValue() const;

  BIND_METHOD()
  void add(int amount);
};
```

Header dependencies and runtime value types follow [Build and Module Layout](<Build and Module Layout.md#core-headers-and-runtime-boundary>). `BIND_METHOD(name = "...")` selects the Lua method name, and it applies to `metadata = false` methods as well.

Place the declaration in the module's `include/Counter.hpp` and the member definitions in `src/Counter.cpp`:

```cpp
#include "Counter.hpp"

Counter::Counter(int initial) : value(initial) {}

int Counter::getValue() const {
  return value;
}

void Counter::add(int amount) {
  value += amount;
}
```

CMake discovers `include/**/*.hpp` and `src/**/*.cpp`. Rebuild the module to regenerate its bindings. For a `Counter` class in `Engine`, Lua code can use:

```lua
local Engine = require("Engine")
local Logging = require("Global.Utils.Logging")

local counter = Engine.Counter.new(4)
counter:add(3)
Logging.info(counter:getValue())
```

The module root is the only public runtime location for the class. The `name` option selects the Lua identifier for that root field. Do not create a second table path for the same native class.

`BIND_CLASS(callbacks = true)` dispatches this class's non-static virtual bound methods through Lua. The opt-in is not inherited, but an override of a base-selected callback remains active.

`BIND_METHOD(callback = false)` excludes the current class's method without removing an inherited callback. Selection is independent of metadata and events. String lists and non-virtual constructor callbacks are unsupported.

Bindgen infers conversion bases from the C++ declaration. `cast_bases = {"BaseA", "BaseB"}` adds ancestors, or supplies them when `bind_bases = false`. The option requires an ordered list of non-empty type names rather than a comma-separated string.

A conversion base with a registered Lua type also contributes its native methods and properties, including on userdata returned directly from C++. Bindgen emits `BindBase` for these bases and `BindCast` for interfaces without a Lua type. `bind_bases = false` disables inference from declared bases; it does not hide members of explicitly supplied registered bases. `runtime_bases` still controls the separate Ludork class composition hierarchy.

Every logical public `BIND_METHOD` enters editor metadata by default. Mark an internal method or a secondary adapter overload as `metadata = false` when it must remain available to native Lua and LuaLS without creating another Blueprint node:

```cpp
BIND_METHOD(metadata = false)
void _updateCache();
```

The flag removes neither the runtime registration nor the LuaLS stub. Method names exposed in metadata must be unique within a type.

### Declare properties

`BIND_PROPERTY()` exposes a data member. Safe boolean, numeric, string and `{}` initialisers can become metadata defaults. Use annotation-native pure data for an explicit default. Put property editor semantics that cannot be inferred from the type inside `BIND_PROPERTY(meta(...))`.

```cpp
BIND_PROPERTY(
    default = {0.0, 0.0})
sf::Vector2f defaultOrigin{0.0f, 0.0f};
```

Positional entries form arrays and named entries form objects. Bindgen reads this annotation syntax directly, so it does not need to be a valid C++ expression. The same singular `default` syntax applies to a getter-backed property declared with `BIND_METHOD(property = ...)`.

Structured pure-data values inside `meta(...)` use the same brace DSL. Either form may be nested:

```cpp
BIND_PROPERTY(
    meta(Rely = {source = "autoSound", op = "!=", value = ""}))
float autoSoundInterval = 0.0f;

BIND_METHOD(defaults = {{}},
            meta(MoveRouteVars = {"route"}),
            outpins(default = nil))
void setRoute(
    const std::optional<std::vector<sf::Vector2i>>& route = {});
```

Use lowercase `true` and `false` in this data. Brace syntax, protocol `nil` and quoted-JSON rejection follow [Macro Reference](<Macro Reference.md>).

Ordinary properties and methods do not declare `DisplayName` or `DisplayDesc`. The editor formats identifiers automatically, so `defaultOrigin` is displayed as `Default Origin` while the C++ and Lua member name remains `defaultOrigin`. A true operator alias may use a direct literal display name such as `+`. It must not use `LOC(...)` or a default description.

A no-argument getter can expose a property:

```cpp
BIND_METHOD(property = "volume", setter = "setVolume")
float getVolume() const;

void setVolume(float value);
```

The getter return type becomes the property type unless `type` overrides it. This form exposes one property and does not also expose getter and setter nodes.

A computed property may also declare `component = true`, preserving the same component metadata as a data member while routing assignment through its setter. `Actor.emitterComp` uses this form to release the previous effect immediately when replaced or assigned `nil`, including while its Actor is dormant.

### Review constructors and exclusions

`BIND_INIT` marks constructors. Leave a declaration without a binding marker when it must not be exposed. Use `BIND_CLASS_PROPERTY` for class-level values and `BIND_MODULE_PROPERTY` for module-level values.

Bound constructors use `.new(...)`. Instance properties access native instance storage; class properties access C++ static storage. A complete record marked `copyable = true` gains `copy()` and `deepcopy()` when all members have verified independent value semantics. Scalars, strings, containers and nested independent values can qualify; pointers, Lua references and shared resources do not become deep-copyable from `copyable` alone. The complete native copy includes private state only when an explicit complete type policy establishes that it is safe.

### Bind scoped enums

Use `BIND_ENUM` when a fixed native value set must be shared with Lua:

```cpp
BIND_ENUM()
enum class WeatherType {
  NONE = 0,
  RAIN = 1,
};
```

Bindgen generates `Module.WeatherType` and its LuaLS type. The native build also generates `Scripts/Enums/Module/WeatherType.lua`, which returns its named integer constants with source annotations. The module retains the `Enums.Module.WeatherType` table type and uses inline annotations to give its members the original `Module.WeatherType` API value type; it has no mirrored enum stub. Blueprint fields and signatures use `{ enum = "Enums.Module.WeatherType" }`; Lua calls and saved Blueprint values retain the underlying integers. Do not duplicate enumerators as module properties. The original native table remains available and shares its compiled values with the pure enum module.

An existing const map can supply a scalar enum without introducing a C++ enum:

```cpp
BIND_MODULE_PROPERTY(enum = true)
extern const std::unordered_map<std::string, int> Direction;
```

Only const maps with string keys and numeric, string or boolean values support this marker. `Engine.Direction` and `Engine.FocusDirection` use it. The generated enum modules are owned by the build; edit the declaration or map source and rebuild.

Use `metadata_type` when an existing scalar property should show an enum selector while keeping its C++ and LuaLS types:

```cpp
BIND_PROPERTY(metadata_type = {enum = "Enums.Engine.Direction"})
int direction = 0;
```

The selector saves the referenced constant's value. Parameter and return overrides follow [Metadata-only signature schemas](<Functions Events and Execution.md#metadata-only-signature-schemas>).

### Bind owner-specific nested types

A public nested struct or enum uses the same binding markers as a top-level declaration:

```cpp
class Owner {
public:
  BIND_CLASS()
  struct Data {
    BIND_PROPERTY()
    int value = 0;
  };
};
```

C++ names this type `Owner::Data`, and Lua exposes it as `Module.Data` or under the name set by `name`. The owner need not be bound, but the nested type must be publicly accessible through every enclosing class. With a public forward declaration and a separate qualified definition, place the binding marker on the complete definition.

Types with the same short C++ name in one module need distinct Lua `name` options.

## Value conversion contracts

Use `BIND_CLASS(table_init = true)` to initialise a fixed record from a Lua table. Supplied non-nil writable properties use their declared codecs. Missing or nil fields retain the C++ defaults. Existing native instances are also accepted. Add `strict_fields = true` to reject unknown fields and non-string keys:

```cpp
BIND_CLASS(table_init = true, strict_fields = true)
struct Limits {
  BIND_PROPERTY()
  std::optional<double> minimum;

  BIND_PROPERTY()
  std::optional<double> maximum;
};
```

`strict_fields` does not make optional fields required.

Use `BIND_CLASS(pure_data = true)` for recursive value containers such as `RuntimeData`. Accepted values and variant conversion rules are covered by [Runtime Value Boundaries](<Runtime Value Boundaries.md#lua-value-conversion>).

`pure_data`, `dynamic_value`, `opaque_identity` and `table_init` are mutually exclusive conversion modes. See [Generated Metadata and Stubs](<Generated Metadata and Stubs.md#defaults-and-types>) for their generated type representations.

## Limitations

Bindgen does not infer project-specific conversion rules or resolve incomplete cross-module types.

## Related pages

- [Generated Metadata and Stubs](<Generated Metadata and Stubs.md>)
- [Macro Reference](<Macro Reference.md>)
- [Runtime Value Boundaries](<Runtime Value Boundaries.md>)
